- Ifthe system proposes a meter reading result then choose one of the following two options:
- If you adopt the meter reading result, the system adds the meter reading reason Move-in to the result.
- If you change the meter reading result, a new result is created with the meter reading reason Move-in .
- Ifthe system does not propose a meter reading result, you can have it estimate a result or enter one manually. In both cases, the system creates a new meter reading result from the adopted/changed result and gives it the meter reading reason Move-In.
- Ifthe system does not propose a meter reading result, and you do not enter one manually, a service notification or service order is created for the current register. For more information see Service notifications and orders.

You can also suppress the meter reading proposal or define an interval as required. If you do this, the system only makes a proposal if the meter reading result on which the proposal is based was takes during the interval. Ensure you have configured the system accordingly in Customizing under |)*SAP Utilities » Device Management » Meter Reading » Basic Settings » Define Control Parameters for Meter Reading Data Processing » . Ensure that you make an appropriate entry in the Move-in prop. inter. (Interval for determining default value) and the Display default move-in value checkbox alongside it. You can find additional information on meter reading data processing in the section on the meter reading component.

Title: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure

Content:
Purpose

Billing uses meter reading results or load profiles to determine the evaluation basis for schema execution. All calculations required for rate creation are made during schema execution. Different billing periods are included in the various billing procedures. All master and billing master data can change during a billing period. The billing module ensures that all billing-relevant changes that occur during a billing period are taken into consideration. For example, a price change causes the system to divide the total period into subperiods, each with the price valid for that subperiod. The system also divides the total consumption, which produces the corresponding partial amount. You can process all known period categories using different billing procedures.

Use

You can use this function to execute billing simulation for a single contract for the entire backbilling and period-end billing period. You may want to do this for testing purposes or to provide customers with information.

Prerequisites

- Backbilling or period-end billing must be active for the contract.
- Thecontract must be billable.

Features

You can perform this function for a single contract. When you do so, the system automatically carries out the following activities:

- The current backbilling and/or period-end billing period is determined for the contract.
- Billing simulation is executed for each billing period that falls within the backbilling and/or period-end billing period. The meter reading results required for the individual billing periods are determined via extrapolation. If meter reading results were already entered for the backbilling and/or period-end billing period, then these are used for the simulation. If actual (period) billings have already been performed in the backbilling and/or period-end billing period, these are also

taken into account; simulation is not executed in these cases.

- The simulation results are displayed in an overview. The following information is processed:
  - Net amount for the entire backbilling and period-end billing period
  - Net amount listed separately for the period billings in the backbilling and period-end billing periods, and for the bill resulting from the period-end billing
  - Net amount for each period billing within the backbilling and/or period-end billing period

Meter reading results and period consumption are displayed per register. From the overview display, you can double-click on the net amounts to branch to the display of individual billing documents (for the period billings or the period-end billing). You can also simulate invoicing for the entire backbilling and/or period-end billing period using the results of the billing simulation. To do so, you must first save (upload) the results of the billing simulation. From the overview of the simulation results, you can execute other simulation runs for the contract. This enables you to change the period consumption per billing period (for the period billings). In this way, the system can generate several simulated versions whose results you can then compare.

setting, meter reading orders are not generated during order creation for dates with estimation. The billing order is given the status Billable; the value Billing Estimates Value from Meter Reading Unit (01) is entered in the Estimated in Billing field.

- If you use DPC with the basic category determination of current periods via meter reading results, you do not have to make any extra settings in scheduling.

As a supplier in a deregulated scenario, you can execute your transactions independently of the distributor’s scheduling. You can organize scheduling based on your billing grid. The system estimates a meter reading result for the billing dates. If the distributor reports a real meter reading result, you enter an interim meter reading with billing. In this billing run, the system corrects the period back to the last real meter reading result.

Content:
You can use the Customer-Specific Fields in Billing Document (EBIAQ001) enhancement if you only want to display dynamic backbillings that have changed amounts (in comparison to the original bill) on the customer’s current bill. This enhancement enables you to specify other lines as not relevant for printing. ee Example

Use

You can use the variants Write DBERCHV Info Lines for Quantities (QUANTI22) and Write Consumption and Amount in Consumption History (QUANTI23) to update consumption amounts to the Consumption History table (DBERCHV). If you want to include consumption values based on estimated meter reading results in the consumption history, you can correct these during dynamic backbilling. In the rate step for the selected variant, select the Reversible for Backbilling value in the VC (variant control) field. In the corresponding schema step, enter a dynamic backbilling group in the field RDP1 to (RDP5) (Schema Steps for Reversal in Dynamic Period Control). An entry is then generated in the DBERCHV table during dynamic backbilling. This entry replaces the original entry. If you enter a dynamic backbilling group in the schema step field SS1 (to SS5) (Schema Steps for Execution in Dynamic Period Control), the consumption for the dynamic backbilling period is updated in the consumption history.

Preconsumption Values in the Billing Document

You can use the variant Write Info Lines for n Previous Consumption Values (QUANTI17) to write information lines about different preconsumption values. Note that the corrected consumption values are not yet saved in the installation facts when this variant is executed during dynamic period control and backbilling. You can determine in variant control that info lines are to be written for the corrected consumptions.

Consumption Values in the Installation Facts

There are two ways of updating consumption values in the installation facts. You must use a time slice generator that has been allocated the following basic categories of the period to be created for the variant that writes the consumption values to the installation facts (for example, Write a Quantity in the Installation Facts (INFACTO6)).

- Display consumption values in the installation facts for each billing period. You require.
  - For the categories 1000 and 2000, a period to be created from the basic category Cycle (4)
  - For categories 3000 and 4000, a period to be created from the Past Time Slices for Each Individual Document (1) basic category and the Cycle (4) basic category
- Display consumption values in the installation facts depending on real meter reading results You require.
  - For the categories 1000 and 2000, a period to be created from the basic category Cycle (4)
  - For categories 3000 and 4000, a period to be created from the Current Period and Past in Congruent Time Slice (3) category.

In the rate step for the variant, choose a variant control that updates values in the billing period. This ensures that the consumption values in the installation facts are corrected during dynamic backbilling.

Content:
As of SAP IS-U release 4.71, you can combine DPC with budget billing amounts. This allows you to collect fixed monthly amounts from customers in the deregulated marketplace, for example. After a period of one year, a new budget billing plan should be created using actual meter reading results. If no actual meter reading result is available, the system creates the new budget billing plan based on an estimated meter reading result. Once the next actual meter reading result is available, you can enter an interim meter reading with billing. The system then corrects the entire period back to the last actual meter reading result. You can choose

Billings that are based on estimated meter reading results must be corrected during the next actual meter reading. The difference between the dynamic backbilled consumption and the consumption from the estimated period must be billed in the current periodic billing period. To do this, update the billed consumption in the facts for any billing periods with estimated meter readings. Choose variant control ,Update Sum in the Future’ For periodic billing based on actual meter reading results, use the time slice generator to determine a period that belongs to period basic category “3” (Current period and past in a congruent time slice). You use variant DYNBIO5 to update the consumption in the periodic billing period and to subtract the consumption from the facts. If the estimations were too high, it is possible that a negative consumption value is billed. Price changes in the dynamic backbilling period, for example, are not taken into account in this procedure. You have the option to copy amounts and consumption values from backbilling periods to the periodic billing period. You use variants DYNBIO4 or DYNBIO5 for this purpose.

In the Real Time Pricing (RTP) interface, values from the Energy Data Management component (IS-U-EDM) are transferred to the Contract Billing component (IS-U-BI). The RTP interface allows you to use the profiles managed in IS-U-EDM directly in IS-U Billing. In order to this, you allocate the RTP interface to the rate used for billing an interval meter. In the RTP interface you can execute billing-relevant processing steps carried out based on profiles. For example, you can process billing agreements for periods as small as 15 minutes. The results of this processing step are then transferred to the rate step of the rate. The bill lines are then created from the rate steps. You can allocate the Formula result parameter to an output parameter. Result parameters describe the results of RTP interface execution. The result parameter values are determined using result functions. You can allocate result parameters to output parameters based on the strucutre defined for the RTP component. This means that you can allocate different result parameters to the output parameter for every possible combination of season type, day type, and time-of-use type. During execution of the RTP interface, a profile is created from the profile values of the allocated output parameter for each result parameter. The profile values of an output parameter can be used by multiple result parameters. Alternatively, one result parameter can be supplied with values from more than one output parameter. The result function allocated to the result parameter is executed for the profile values transferred to the result parameter. You can allocate different result parameters to one output parameter in different RTP components. These result parameters are then processed according to the priority of the RTP component and corresponding activation periods.

Content:
synthetic Profile Adjusted to Period Consumption for the Interval Meter

Time-of-Use Simulation Rules

To simulate rate steps, access billing in the simulation mode or perform periodic billing with integrated budget billing simulation. You access the transaction for individual billing simulation in the SAP menu under !®Utilities Industrv ® Billing ® Billing

To ensure simulation is as accurate as possible, note the following:

- If you archive profile values quickly (short residence time) they are no longer available for simulation of billing for time-of-use rates. This reduces the accuracy of the simulation.
- Enter the period consumption for interval meters during move-in.
- Inthe time-of-use interface, use a consumption pattern (and a synthetic profile) that best suits the customer.
- If you create a contract in a vacant status period, for example, with the owner of a rented apartment, we recommend that you implement BAd| ISU_FASTEDM TOU SIMULATION, method DETERMINE CONTRACTS.

More Information

For more detailed information about the simulation process flow, see the system documentation TOU Simulation, which you can access from a link in the description of the field Consumption Pattern (F1 Help) in the time-of-use interface.

Within an advanced metering infrastructure, consumption profiles are managed in an external meter data unification and synchronization (MDUS) system. This involves a considerable volume of data, in particular for residential customers. Such granularity of data is not necessary for consumption billing in the SAP system. You can use the time-of-use interface to import aggregated profile values into the SAP system so that they can be processed by the rate.

- The business function Advanced Metering Infrastructure 2 (ISU AMI_2) is active.
- You are familiar with the basics of billing (see Contract Billing) and the advanced metering structure (see Advanced Metering Infrastructure).

To ensure that the profile values in the MDUS system can be aggregated for the MDUS request, the interval length of the time-of-

In the example above the year is divided into summer and winter. In summer you can choose from weekdays, weekends, public holidays, and exception days (such as the football world cup final day). Whilst for weekdays, consumption and demand are calculated using other formulas based on the time of day, only consumption is calculated for weekends. You can define how the year can be divided into sections in Customizing. You can also map the year as a season group, or as a group with the season types summer, winter, and transition. For each season, you determine in the time-of-use interface, the type of day (Monday-Sunday, public holiday, exception day) on which you expect consumption behaviour to be different. These are the Day Groups. In contrast to the example, you could also group Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays, and exception days into a Non- Working Days day group. In the day group for a season, you then define the times at which to use certain formulas. The consumption periods are managed historically. For example, if you change the consumption period Summer, Weekday, 00:00-07:59 to 00:00-08:29, the change date is noted. From this date, the changed period is then used for the MDUS request and for billing.

The result parameter connects the time-of-use interface and the rate. The operands use these parameters to get the values during billing. Result parameters can include multiple output parameters. In the example, the result parameter OFFPEAK adds together the consumption on weekdays to 07:59 and from 18:00, and the entire consumption at weekends, and transferres the total to the operand CONS OFFPEAK. The result parameter can also transfer minimum and maximum values to an operand instead of the total. In the example, the result parameter DEM MAX transfers the maximum demand for weekdays between 08:00 and 17:59. For more information, see:\Map Consumption Times from Time-of-Use Interface in Rate

You have to make settings for the time-of-use interface in Customizing for Contract Billing under |)Billing Master Data > AMI: Time-of-Use Interface ‘). This includes the settings for the time-of-use formula.

Content:
The billing schema extension is an entity in SAP IS-U contract billing that is integrated in the billing schema according to the data model. The billing schema extension contains the conditional billing program and the rate relationship group with the rate relationships. You establish which rates are billed and the order in which they are to be processed in the billing schema. You define the relationship between these rates in the billing schema extension: Which rates are used as basic rates for the entire billing period and which rates are only used as conditional rates for active TOU exceptions to supplement or substitute the basic rates. Basic rates and conditional rates must be used in the same schema and be defined with the same relationship in rate determination. The conditional billing program defined in the billing schema extension is used to activate conditional rates. Assigning conditional billing programs to TOU exception programs executes the corresponding rates in the billing schema extension for an active TOU exception.

More Information

Rate Relationships

Conditional Billing Program

Activities

Create Billing Schema Extension

The conditional billing program is used to activate conditional rates for an active TOU exception. You define the conditional billing program in the billing schema extension and assign it to TOU exception programs. The conditional billing program refers to a billing schema. You also assign conditional rates to the conditional billing program. These assignments mean the system executes the corresponding conditional rates for the billing schema extension for an active TOU exception. The conditional billing program means rates can be controlled with a greater degree of flexibility during an exception period. You can assign the conditional billing program to several rate relationship groups and several TOU exception programs. This gives you several options for representing specific contract conditions and different types of rates including those for interval customers.

Content:
A time-of-use exception is an activation of a TOU exception program for a specific period and is described using the following attributes:

- Start of activation (date and time)
- End of activation
- Reference to the TOU exception program activated

In addition to the TOU exception, additional information about specific customers is required according to the activation category for the TOU exception program. This information is defined as a time-of-use exception response. The TOU exception response has the following attributes:

- Logical register number
- Reference to TOU exception
- Response category The response category can have one of the following statuses:
  - Opt-in The TOU exception is to be taken into account as active during billing.
  - Opt-out The TOU exception is not to be taken into account during billing.

Activating a TOU exception program in billing for a contract is dependent on the interaction of the TOU exception and the TOU exception response. A TOU exception response can be optional or mandatory according to the activation category of the TOU exception program. If the user wants to make a correction at contract level, for example to deactivate a TOU exception for a specific contract, they can create a TOU exception response with a suitable response category for the TOU exception in the system.

Use

Critical peak prices (Critical Peak Pricing - CPP) are billed in part by using calculation algorithms that extend beyond simply aggregating consumption values during a TOU exception. The objective here is to offer customers a financial incentive to reduce their consumption during a TOU exception period. In addition to applying higher prices during the exception period, discounts are also granted to customers who have actually successfully reduced their consumption. When using the model rebates at critical peak load times (Peak Time Rebate — PTR), consumption during the exception period is compared with comparable péeriods in the past. Past consumption is usually represented as an arithmetic average across several comparison periods.

The formula class that supports critical peak prices CL_ISU FASTEDM FORMULA CPP contains an algorithm that calculates the actual consumption for a time-of-use exception period including past periods. These quantities are available from the results parameters of formula execution in the billing process as operand values and can be used in rate calculations. The algorithm in this formula represents a typical CPP rate. You can use this TOU formula as a basis for additional project-specific formula implementations.

More Information

1 Define time-of-use exception programs. You use TOU exception programs for example to represent demand response programs in the SAP IS-U system. TOU exception programs bundle TOU exceptions and create the connection between the conditional billing program and the

TOU exception. For more information, see Defining Time-of-Use Exception Programs

2 Design rate constructs for conditional billing. a. Define the rates that you want to use as basic rates and those that you want to use as conditional rates. Use the rates in a corresponding schema and in rate determination. Select the Execute Conditional Billing Program indicator in the schema and the rate category.

Note You can usé a billing schema for which this indicator is selected, in a rate category for which this indicator is not selected. If you do so however, the system ignores all conditional rates for the billing schema extension during billing. b. Select the Assignment to a Conditional Rate Allowed indicator in the time-of-use interface. This enables the time-of-use interface to be assigned to a rate that is to be used as a conditional rate in a billing schema extension.

3 Create billing schema extensions for the schemas. For more information, see

Create Billing Schema Extension

4 Define conditional billing programs in the billing schema extension and assign them to TOU exception programs. Assigning conditional billing programs to TOU exception programs executes the corresponding rates in the billing schema extension for an active TOU exception.
5 Define rate relationships between basic rates and conditional rates in the billing schema extension.

You define TOU exception programs in Customizing in the activity Define Time-of-Use Exception Program. Content:
You monitor and edit TOU exceptions and the associated TOU exception responses on a daily basis. You can use the following transactions to do so, for which more information is available from the respective link below:

- Monitor and Edit Time-of-Use Exceptions
- Monitor and Edit Time-of-Use Exception Responses

To reduce your database load, you can archive TOU exceptions and exception responses.

Dynamic Period Control Dynamic period control enables flexible billing where, in a deregulated scenario, actual meter reading results are no longer stored in a grid defined in scheduling, but can be exchanged between utility companies at any time. In the billing schema, you can use the time slice generator to create individual correction periods. You can do the following, for example:

- Recalculate consumption prices from the billing document while leaving the rental price unchanged.
- Define which billing steps are carried out for actual meter reading results and which are carried out for estimated meter reading results.
- Choose whether a correction is carried out over the entire correction period, or only for individual partial correction periods.
- Execute advance billing, which the system can recalculate automatically.

You can use a simulation period to generate extrapolated posting-relevant billing line items in dynamic period control, or information lines in the billing document, and correct them in subsequent billing runs. This allows you to present any extrapolation periods to your customers on the bill.

Title: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure
Section: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure > Processing Meter Reading Data in Dynamic Period Control
Document: doc_011

Content:
You can use the following enhancements and programs for processing meter reading data for dynamic period control (DPC).

Enhancement:Customer-Specific, Independent Validation

If you use DPC with the basic category Determination of Current Periods via Meter Reading Results , you can use the Customer- Specific, Independent Validation enhancement (EDMLELDV) to implement an individual validation. This check determines if the current real meter reading results is greater than the last real meter reading result. For more information, see SAP note 398471.

Programs

- Use the Deactivation for Individual Installation program ( RELDELEB) if you have set the Estim. in Bill. indicator but real meter reading results already exist for the date selected. This generates meter reading orders for the billing order. In the billing order, the value in the Estim. in Bill. field changes from Billing Estimates Value from Meter Reading Unit (01) to Billing Does Not Estimate Value Deleted by Individual report(04) .
- Use the Activation for Individual Installation program (RELSETEB) ifEstim. in Bill. is not maintained and there are no meter reading results available for the periodic meter reading date. The existing meter reading orders are deleted; the

value in the Estimated in Billing field changes to Billing Estimates Value Changed by Individual Report (03) .

- The Activation for Multiple Installations program (RELSETEBMASS) executes the changes described above for all installations that do not have any real meter reading results in an interval.

Title: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure
Section: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure > Executing DPC Billing
Document: doc_011

Content:
Real Meter Reading Results

If you want to use DPC with the basic category Determination of Current Periods via Meter Reading Results , dynamic backbilling must be executed every time a real meter reading result is entered. If it is not, meter overflows occur whenever the last estimated meter reading result in the Meter Reading Results table (EABL) is higher than the current real meter reading result that you have entered.

ee Example You enter real meter reading results during a meter replacement. The previous interim meter reading was estimated. You can use the Invoicing Grouping (R403) event to group the interim billing run and the next periodic billing run together on one bill.

Estimated Meter Reading Results

Caution If you use DPC with the basic category Estimation of Meter Reading Results in Billing , you should not save the estimated meter reading results in the Meter Reading Results table (EABL). Otherwise, you lose the benefits DPC with the basic category Estimation of Meter Reading Results in Billing has over DPC with the basic categoryDetermination of Current Periods via Meter Reading Results. In this case, you would have to perform dynamic backbilling for each real meter reading result entered, so as to avoid meter overflows.

Floating Backbilling

You can use DPC with the basic category Estimation of Meter Reading Results in Billing to execute floating backbilling to the last real meter reading result. To do this, you must select a period to be created from the basic period category Current Period and Past in a Congruent Time Slice for all categories of schema steps for which you want to execute floating backbilling.

Caution If you use dynamic period control from the basic category Estimation of Meter Reading Results in Billing , you should never print estimated meter reading results on a bill.

This could have been caused, for example, by a device replacement or an interim meter reading.

Alternative Portion

If an alternative portion is defined in a contract, you can use variant QUANTI26 ( Simulate Billing Period ) to create a billing document until the scheduled meter reading date for the alternative portion. This means that all of a customer’s contracts can be billed for the same period. The meter reading for the meter reading date of the alternative portion is extrapolated in the variant. The system then simulates a document up to the scheduled meter reading date. In the variant control, you can specify whether the document lines of the simulation document are transferred to the current billing document. For further information about the control options, see the documentation for variant QUANTI26.

Dynamic Backbilling

You can use several variant programs to execute dynamic backbilling. In these variant programs, dynamic backbilling is executed for schema steps that contain a dynamic backbilling group from the DYNBI step. The variant programs have different backbilling periods. If you maintain the dynamic backbilling group in one of the fields SDP1 to SDP5 (schema steps for reversal in dynamic period control), the amounts from the posting-relevant lines these schema steps generated in previous billing documents are transferred to the current document as negative amounts. If you maintain the dynamic backbilling group in the Schema Step for Dynamic Period Control , the period that you allocated to the time slice generator for the current category is dynamically backbilled. You can use the following variant programs for dynamic backbilling:

- DYNBIO1 executes dynamic backbilling back to the last real meter reading result
- DYNBIO2 dynamically backbills the schema steps from the previous document
- DYNBIO3 dynamically backbills schema steps from the last dynamic backbilling
- DYNBIO4 updates amounts from the correction periods in the billing period

For further information, see the documentation on the individual variants.

Content:
Purpose

Process Flow

The billing of interval-related data (profiles) is called real time pricing billing (RTP billing). RTP billing allows you to define rates and prices freely across intervals and therefore enables you to structure contracts that are required in a deregulated energy market more freely. RTP billing is based on rate models that evaluate energy requirements over a period of time. Consumption (and demand if necessary) are measured for each interval (for example %4-hour, ¥2-hour) or for each rate period (for example peak and off-peak). The price for kWh of consumption, or kW/kWA demand is determined for every interval. This means the price may vary for every interval. You can use RTP billing to calculate time-of-use pricing models and RTP models. You can define prices in advance or adjust prices to the spot price defined by the energy market. Time-of-use pricing models are time-based. This means that prices are determined based on time groups.

Example for Time-of-Use Pricing ® Different prices depending on time blocks such as time of day, day type (week day, weekend day) or season type (summer, winter)

RTP models are quantity-based. This means that prices are determined based on agreed reference quantities.

Content:
Formula Definition

You can allocate input parameters to calculation modes in the transaction for defining formulas. You must define one calculation mode as a default value for the parameter.

1 Select (double click) an input parameter from the list. The parameter number of the selected parameter appears automatically in the Calculation Mode group box.
2 Select one of the predefined calculation modes in the Calc.Mode (calculation mode) field.
3 If you want the system to use this calculation mode as the default value for the parameter, select the Default Value field. Only ever select the Default Value field for one calculation mode.
4 Choose @yCopy. Your entries are then transferred to the list.
5 Repeat the steps whenever you want to allocate one or more calculation modes to input parameters.

Formula Calculation

You use a function module to calculate formulas. Before defining any extra formulas in addition to those predefined by SAP, you must define a function module for the calculations. To define formulas, go to Customizing for SAP Utilities and choose |+Tools System Modifications User-Defined Enhancements for Energy Data Management » Formulas. In the function modules, you can respond to the calculation modes of the individual intervals in order to influence the results of formula calculation.

You can use the formulas described in the source text to copy a quantity profile and convert it into a demand profile. Input parameter:

- Quantity profile

Output parameters:

- Copy of quantity profile
- Copy of demand profile (demand)

Only those quantity profile values with calculation mode O1 ( Value Included in Calculation ) are copied and converted. The demand value is set to zero for the remaining calculation modes. The default value of the input parameter is used for every interval in the billing period. In enhancement EEDMFOOI, you can set any calculation mode for each interval based on the status of the input profile value, for example. For each input parameter, you can use variable xmod<n> to activate the calculation mode in the function module.

Enhancement EEDMFOO1

You can use this enhancement to determine the calculation mode of profile values for calculating formulas. The enhancement contains function module EXIT_SAPLEEDM_FORMUTIL_OO1. In this function module, you can determine the calculation mode given to the values of a profile for formula calculation. The dates in the parameters are all given in UTC time. This also applies to the parameters in table format. If you need the dates in the enhancement to be in local time, you have to convert them. You can do this using the macros defined in include IEEDM_TIMCVT.

ee Example This example implementation of enhancement EEDMFOO1 determines the periods, in which the status of the profile values was set to Interpolated or Extrapolated . The calculation mode of the periods is set to 02 — Value Not Included in Calculation .

- Copy of demand profile (demand)

Only those quantity profile values with calculation mode O1 ( Value Included in Calculation ) are copied and converted. The demand value is set to zero for the remaining calculation modes. The default value of the input parameter is used for every interval in the billing period. In enhancement EEDMFOOI, you can set any calculation mode for each interval based on the status of the input profile value, for example. For each input parameter, you can use variable xmod<n> to activate the calculation mode in the function module.

Enhancement EEDMFOO1

You can use this enhancement to determine the calculation mode of profile values for calculating formulas. The enhancement contains function module EXIT_SAPLEEDM_FORMUTIL_OO1. In this function module, you can determine the calculation mode given to the values of a profile for formula calculation. The dates in the parameters are all given in UTC time. This also applies to the parameters in table format. If you need the dates in the enhancement to be in local time, you have to convert them. You can do this using the macros defined in include IEEDM_TIMCVT.

ee Example This example implementation of enhancement EEDMFOO1 determines the periods, in which the status of the profile values was set to Interpolated or Extrapolated . The calculation mode of the periods is set to 02 — Value Not Included in Calculation .

The activation type Use and Activate Generally (activation and definition for all installations) means that you have to activate the RTP components at RTP interface level and define the parameter allocations for the input parameters at RTP interface level.

Activation type "Use and Activate Individually"

The activation type Use and Activate Individually (activation for individual installations) means that you cannot activate the RTP components at RTP interface level, but at installation level.

- You can define parameter templates at RTP interface level and then use these templates to define the parameter allocations for the input parameters at installation level.

Activation type "Use and Activate Generally"

The activation type "Use Individually and Activate Generally" (activation for all installations and for individual installations) means that you have to activate the RTP components at RTP interface level and at installation level. You have the following options for defining the parameter allocations for the input parameters:

- You can define the parameter allocations at RTP interface level
- You can define parameter templates at RTP interface level and then use these templates to define the parameter allocations for the input parameters at installation level.

Example You have activated component 1 at RTP interface level with activation type Use and Activate Generally and assigned it priority 2. As aresult, component 1 is valid for all installations to which this RTP interface is allocated. You have made a contractual agreement with a number of customers regarding a special delivery within a certain period of time. You wantto map this agreement using component 2. To do this, activate component 2 with priority 1 at RTP interface level for the period in which the special delivery is to take place, and choose activation type Use Individually and Activate Generally. Also activate component 2 at installation level of each individual customer for the validity period of the contract.

Title: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure
Section: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure > Consumption Billing Based on Profile Values in the SAP System
Document: doc_011

Content:
Use

Within an advanced metering infrastructure, consumption profiles are managed in a meter data unification and synchronization (MDUS) system. You can import the profile values into the SAP system from the MDUS system for further processing in consumption billing. We recommend that you use the time-of-use (TOU) interface for consumption billing, and the procedure described below uses the TOU interface. For more information about using the RTP interface, see RTP Billing.

Prerequisites

The business function Advanced Metering Infrastructure 2 (ISU_AMI_ 2) is active. You are familiar with the basics of billing (see Contract Billing) and importing profile values (see Energy Data Management). If you want to use the TOU interface for consumption billing based on profile values in the SAP system, you must select the indicator Profile Can Be Billed with TOU Interface for these profiles. The profiles must meet the following conditions:

- The profile category that belongs to the profile type is Elementary Profile.
- The interval length ID has the value 05, 10, 15, 30, or 60.
- The profile value category has the value Quantity or Demand.
- The profile is not allocated a replacement value procedure group.
- The profile is not allocated a consistency check group.
- The day offset has the value 00:00:00.
- The Cumulative Values indicator is not selected.

The profile values must have one of the following statuses:

- Value is valid (IUO12)
- Value was estimated (IU013)
- Value entered/changed manually (IUO15)
- Value was extrapolated (IUO20)
- Value was interpolated (IU021)
- Value manually changed externally (IUO22)

Billing Procedure

1 You define a time-of-use interface and select it for execution in EDM. You use time-of-use formulas with a formula class. SAP provides formula classes for aggregation and determination of peak demand values. You can also define your own formula classes.
2 You import the profile values in the SAP system - for example, using BAP! BAPI_ISUPROFILE IMPORT.
3 You execute billing as normal.

Constraints

Billing in combination with period-end billing, backbilling, or billing in advance is only possible with restrictions. Operands that receive values from the time-of-use interface can only be used in rate steps that belong to the periodic billing period.

Content:
In the example above the year is divided into summer and winter. In summer you can choose from weekdays, weekends, public holidays, and exception days (such as the football world cup final day). Whilst for weekdays, consumption and demand are calculated using other formulas based on the time of day, only consumption is calculated for weekends. You can define how the year can be divided into sections in Customizing. You can also map the year as a season group, or as a group with the season types summer, winter, and transition. For each season, you determine in the time-of-use interface, the type of day (Monday-Sunday, public holiday, exception day) on which you expect consumption behaviour to be different. These are the

The consumption periods are managed historically. For example, if you change the consumption period Summer, Weekday, 00:00 07:59 to 00:00 08:29, the change date is noted. From this date, the changed period is used for billing. If you have specified in the Execution of Time-of-Use Interface field that you want to use the time-of-use interface in billing for profiles whose values are stored in the SAP system, you must use formulas based on formula classes. In this case, the billing process calls the methods implemented in the formula class.

The result parameter connects the time-of-use interface and the rate. The operands use these parameters to get the values during billing. Result parameters can include multiple output parameters. In the example, the result parameter OFFPEAK adds together the consumption on weekdays to 07:59 and from 18:00, and the entire consumption at weekends, and transferres the total to the operand CONS OFFPEAK. The result parameter can also transfer minimum and maximum values to an operand instead of the total. In the example, the result parameter DEM MAX transfers the maximum demand for weekdays between 08:00 and 17:59. For more information, seeMap Consumption Times from Time-of-Use Interface in Rate

This section explains the numbered elements of the figure above: . Billing order You use the appropriate order creation transactions in the Meter Reading menu. The SAP system creates the orders as follows:

  - Billing orders for all installations regardless of whether the installation contains registers for meter reading reading results (mainly conventional meters) or registers with profile values from the MDUS system (advanced meters).
  - Meter reading orders, only if the installation also contains registers for meter reading results

Regarding whether billing orders can be billed: For installations containing advanced meters, the status of the billing order is supplemented by the MDUS status. The status of the billing order refers to registers for meter reading results. The MDUS status shows whether aggregated values are available in the SAP system for registers with profile values stored in the MDUS system. The initial value of the MDUS status is Request Must Be Created. For installations containing interval registers only, the billing order always has the status Billable; this means that the MDUS status determines whether the order can be billed. . MDUS request You use the appropriate transactions in the Billing menu. The aim of the MDUS request is to aggregate the data and import it into the SAP system so that it can be processed by the rate operands. a. The SAP system determines the individual request items for the billing period for the MDUS system. In the same way as with billing itself, the billing order is analyzed using all billing-relevant data (for example, installation structure, installation facts, rate category, rate, time-of-use interface with periods and formulas, and price changes). A prerequisite is that the installation is billable except for the missing consumption values. b. The SAP system uses an enterprise service to send the MDUS request asynchronously to the MDUS system. The MDUS status of the billing order is Request Sent.

The SAP system only selects the billing orders with the MDUS status Request Confirmed Successfully, and processes them as follows: a. The SAP system checks whether the results of the MDUS request match the billing order, or whether the billing relevant data has changed. =» Nochange: The billing order is billed. Document: doc_011

Content:
You can only perform a billing simulation for profile values in an external system for billing orders for which billing is possible. Other forms of simulation (such as unbilled revenue reporting or budget billing) are only possible for profile values that have been saved in the SAP System. Billing in combination with period-end billing, backbilling, or billing in advance is only possible with restrictions. Operands that receive values from the MDUS request can only be used in rate steps that belong to the periodic billing period.

Content:
Simulation is performed according to the following rules that apply to all profile time slices that are assigned to a time-of-use rate in the simulation period:

Zero values in disconnection period

synthetic profile adjusted to billed annual consumption

synthetic profile adjusted to period consumption of interval meter

Time-of-Use Simulation Rules for Externally Saved Profile Values

Step 1: Zero Values in Disconnection Period

The billing program checks whether the interval meter has been disconnected during the simulation period. The system observes disconnections with the disconnection statuses 02 - Lowered/lLimited and03 - Disconnected. It is assumed that the disconnection period has zero consumption, meaning that the profile values are set to zero.

Step 2: Adjust Synthetic Profile to Measured Annual Consumption

For the remaining simulation period, the system uses a synthetic profile to generate the profile values. The synthetic profile is determined using the consumption pattern specified in the time-of-use interface. The synthetic profile has a standardized annual consumption and therefore has to be adjusted to the annual consumption of the customer. The billing program attempts to determine the measured annual consumption for the profile by aggregating the existing measured total consumptions from MDUS requests. The system uses MDUS requests from the representative period according to the percentage minimum share in the rate. Changes to the period consumption mean that consumptions from MDUS requests from older periods are not used.

Note You can use the method DETERMINE_CONTRACTS in the BADI ISU_FASTEDM_TOU_SIMULATION to influence the contract periods from which MDUS requests can be observed.

Aggregation of the total consumption from MDUS requests does not have to take place for an entire year, but is based ona percentage minimum share in the rate. The synthetic profile is also used for the extrapolation of aggregated consumption values for a year.

Step 3: Synthetic Profile Adjusted to Period Consumption of Interval Meter

To simulate rate steps, access billing in the simulation mode or perform periodic billing with integrated budget billing simulation. You access the transaction for individual billing simulation in the SAP menu under |}Utilities Industry » Billing » Billing Execution Individual Processing » Individual Simulation » Billing i Note To ensure simulation is as accurate as possible, note the following:

- Inthe time-of-use interface, use a consumption pattern (and a synthetic profile) that best suits the customer consumption situation.
- Enter the period consumption for interval meters during move-in.
- Enter a percentage minimum share that is as large as possible in the rate.
- If you create a contract in a vacant status period, for example, with the owner of a rented apartment, we recommend that you implement BAdI ISU_LFASTEDM_TOU_SIMULATION, method DETERMINE_CONTRACTS.

Document: doc_011

Content:
This section describes the technical requirements for contract billing based on profile values in an MDUS system:

- Business Function: The business function Advanced Metering Infrastructure 2 (ISU _AMI_ 2) is active.
- Enterprise Services for MDUS Request:
  - UtilitiesTimeSeriesCalculationERPBulkCreateRequest Out transfers the request items to the MDUS system.
  - UtilitiesTimeSeriesCalculationERPBulkCreateConfirmation In sends the results of the request items back to the SAP system.
  - UtilitiesTimeSeriesCalculationERPCancellationBulkRequest_ Out repeats the MDUS request. That is, it reverses an existing request and sends a new one.
- Business Add-Ins (BAdlIs):
  - ISU _MDUS_ FORMULA enables additional consistency checks for the time-of-use formula.
  - ISU MDUS_IFACE enables additional consistency checks for the time-of-use interface.

Title: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure
Section: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure > Time-of-Use Exceptions and Conditional Billing
Document: doc_011

Content:
The prerequisites for processing time-of-use exceptions and conditional billing are as follows:

- Consumption data in the form of time series

The following process overview shows the processing of time-of-use exceptions and conditional billing in the overall context. Conditional billing itself takes place in SAP IS-U. Some previous process steps are covered by other applications of the SAP for Utilities solution, or they run in external systems.

Note The interfaces between the SAP system and the external systems are not all available as standard and have to be developed as part of the customer project.

Process Overview Part 1: Participation in Time-of-Use Exception Programs and Registration of Customers

1 The customer participates in a time-of-use exception program (SAP DSM). This can be done by selling a corresponding product, for example, via utilities sales management.
2 Participation is implicitly determined by the customer’s rate. As a result, contract billing in SAP IS-U takes the TOU exception program into account.
3 Other external systems (such as Demand Response Management systems - DRMS from third parties) are informed about the customer's registration.

Process Overview Part 2: Activation of Time-of-Use Exceptions for Time-of-Use Exception Programs

1 Certain events require activation of a TOU exception program. These events could be forecasted extreme weather situations or technical problems such as power outages, which result in high consumption peaks.
2 Optimization processes in external systems (DRMS) evaluate a suitable timeframe for a time-of-use exception and select a TOU exception program as well as customers to participate in the TOU exception.
3 Customers, smart meters, and relevant IT systems are informed of the timeframe of the planned TOU exception by the external system.
4 Customers or smart meters provide a response regarding participation in the TOU exception; TOU exception responses are exchanged and logged.
5 TOU exception data and TOU exception response data is stored in SAP IS-U.
6 Consumption data in the form of time series is required for IS-U billing. This data is either uploaded and saved in SAP IS- U/EDM or managed in the MDUS system.

Process Overview Part 3: Conditional Billing

Consumption billing takes place taking TOU exceptions into account (conditional billing).

Conditional billing in SAP IS-U is made possible by the interaction of various entities from the areas of Customizing, master data and transaction data. These entities are listed in the following table. The links in the column More Information provide more detailed concept descriptions.

Title: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure
Section: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure > Time-of-Use Exceptions and Conditional Billing > Use
Document: doc_011

Content:
The on-going rollout of smart meters and the introduction of demand response programs provide an ideal environment for utility companies in an advanced metering infrastructure to improve their load balancing. Contractually agreed participation of customers in demand response programs means that utility companies can use events to react quickly to potential load fluctuations. Special time-of-use rates, which take event-driven dynamic elements into account, offer customers financial incentives to reduce their consumption in critical peak times or to shift their consumption to less critical times. Dynamic elements in the rate model can be, for example, critical peak prices within Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) or Peak Time Rebates (PTR).

Content:
With the processing of time-of-use exceptions and conditional billing, SAP IS-U supports utilities in using these advantages of an advanced metering infrastructure. Demand response programs are mapped in SAP IS-U as time-of-use exception programs; events that occur during demand response programs are referred to as time-of-use exceptions. Time-of-use exceptions are the dynamic elements. They can occur at any time and are typically short in duration (< 1 day). Alternative or additional billing rules need to be applied for the duration of a time-of-use exception. This is done using conditional billing, which is an enhancement of SAP IS-U Billing. Conditional billing can also be used to bill critical peak prices during Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) or to clear peak-time rebates (PTR). Entities in SAP IS-U

Billing Schema Extension

Description

The billing schema extension consists of a group of rates and rate relationships. Conditional rates are activated by conditional billing programs. Assigning conditional billing programs to time-of-use exception programs, executes the corresponding rates in the billing schema extension for active time-of-use exceptions. Use

In conditional billing, the relationship between rates plays a very important role. Rates are used as basic rates for the entire billing period. They are only used as conditional rates for active time-of-use exceptions in order to supplement or substitute the basic rates. Rate relationships between basic rates and conditional rates are defined in the billing schema extension.

Rate Relationship Groups

The rate relationship group specifies a rate fact group to combine a basic rate with all conditional rates that are assigned to this

Rate Relationships

The relationship between basic rates and conditional rates is defined using the rate relationship category:

- Inthe case of the rate relationship category Supplement, the conditional rate is executed in addition to the basic rate.
- Inthe case of the rate relationship category Substitute, the basic rate processes the result of the TOU interface without the TOU exception period. Instead, the system executes the TOU interface of the conditional rate for the TOU exception period. The result is processed in the rate steps for the conditional rate.

Therefore, the basic rate is executed in normal TOU periods and for the rate relationship Supplement during TOU exception periods. The conditional rate is only executed during TOU exception periods. TOU and RTP rates refer to rates that can be used for interval meters and that belong to RTP billing category EDM Profile Values, Bill External Profile Values Using TOU Interface (= TOU rate), or Bill EDM Profile Values Using RTP Interface (= RTP rate). Title: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure
Section: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure > Processing Rate Components > Rate Proration
Document: doc_011

Content:
During billing execution, the rates are first determined by rate determination and prorated for the billing period. In conditional billing, this takes places for the basic rates as well as for the conditional rates. An additional proration takes place for the conditional rates as they do not cover the entire billing period. The propration principle is based on the smallest to-the-day container. The periods in these containers are processed as valid periods. Any other periods that do not contain TOU exceptions are no longer taken into account in conditional billing. The smallest to-the-day containers are determined as follows:

- Thestart of the to-the-day container is the day on which the TOU exception takes place. If the TOU exception ends on the same day, the container contains one day only.
- Ifthe TOU exception lasts longer than one day, the end point of the container is the day on which the TOU exception ends. The to-the-day container contains multiple days.
- If multiple TOU exceptions take place on the same day, the smallest to-the-day containers for the TOU exceptions are grouped into one container. The container contains one day.
- If multiple TOU exceptions take place on consecutive days, and none of the exceptions last longer than one day, multiple separate to-the-day containers are determined, each containing one day.
- If multiple TOU exceptions take place on consecutive days and the exceptions do last longer than one day so that one TOU exception ends on the same day as another starts, the smallest to-the-day containers are grouped together. The start of

the grouped to-the-day container is the day on which the first TOU exception occurs; the end of the grouped to-the-day container is the day on which the last TOU exception ends. The following example illustrates the most important cases:

31.01, 01.01.

Rate Proration

The billing period in the example is the month of January. Eight time-of-use exceptions (red boxes in the graphic) take place in the billing period. These exception periods are:

- TOU exception 1:17.01 9am to 10am
- TOU exception 2: 17.01 1lam to 12pm
- TOU exception 3:17.01 7pm to llpm
- TOU exception 4: 17.01 10pm to 1lpm
- TOU exception 5:17.01 7am to 2pm
- TOU exception 6: 21.01 1pm to 22.01 - 1.30pm
- TOU exception 7: 22.01 2pm to 23.01 - 6.45pm
- TOU exception 8: 24.01 9am to 1.15pm

These time slices result in the following split in billing into the five smallest to-the-day containers T1 to T5 (orange boxes in the graphic): Tl contains three TOU exceptions from one day. T1, T2 and T3 are not grouped together even though they take place on consecutive days. This is because TOU exceptions 1 3, 4 and 5 take place on different days and none of them last longer than one day. T4 contains multiple days and includes TOU exceptions 6 and 7, which do last longer than one day, whereby the end of TOU 6 and the start of TOU 7 are both on the 22.01. T5 contains TOU exception 8. The smallest to-the-day containers provide the basis for further processing.

Title: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure
Section: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure > Processing Rate Components > Variant Programs and Schema Structure
Document: doc_011

Content:
With regard to variant programs that are used in conditional rates and basic rates, there are few absolute restrictions. However, not all constellations yield usable results from a technical and business point of view. You should therefore make sure that billing schemas are technically and functionally set up properly for conditional billing. Take the following recommendations into account.

Period Control

In conditional billing, period control plays an important role in valuating the different billing values represented by the operands. Make sure that you take the special features of period determination and period control into account when maintaining schemas. In billing, conditional rates are always prorated in the smallest to-the-day containers. This means that the rate and the respective billing components are no longer valid for the entire billing period. However, some variant programs require the entire billing period to be covered (for example, IF variants). If both operands cover different times, processing is terminated. This can happen, for example, if for a comparison of two operand values, an operand has been defined for the entrie period while the other operand has been defined for a conditional rate that contains gaps.

Use of Variant Programs

When using variant programs for conditional billing, check whether the variants and their rates make sense from a technical and application point of view. This applies particularly for complicated billing procedures such as backbilling or DPC, as well as for the following points:

- Price block adjustment
- Use of TQUANT
- Physical values such as cosinus phi
- Consumption history
- (Previous) period consumption or demand
- Updating statistics

In the context menu (right click on an output operand), you can choose to display all of an output operand's schema steps that are affected by the operand update in order to analyze the flow of data for operands in schema maintenance. This can be useful for large and complicated schemas. With conditional billing, you can also define new scenarios. When defining the conditional rates, you can use the following variant programs:

- QUANT1A4X: Update for Quantity
- DEMANIA4X: Update for Demand
- COMPUI1X: Update for Amount

These variant programs generate info line items for individual TOU exceptions for a specific time. For more information, see the system documentation for the variant programs.

Use

You represent demand response programs in SAP IS-U as time-of-use exception programs. Events that occur during demand response programs are referred to as time-of-use exceptions. A time-of-use exception program (TOU exception program) groups time-of-use exceptions that belong to the same demand response program. The participation of a customer in a TOU exception program is part of the contractual agreement between the utilities company and the customer. TOU exception programs represent the connection between conditional billing and the TOU exception.

Structure

You define TOU exception programs in Customizing and this definition has the following sections:

Headers: (not detected in source)

in an external system (such as a demand response system).

Ability to split TOU exceptions | Indicator that controls whether TOU exceptions that exceed the

billing period are to be observed proportionally during billing.

Activation category | Logic used to activate TOU exceptions for a TOU exception program

in SAP IS-U billing.

Ability to Split TOU Exceptions

If you select this indicator in Customizing for a TOU exception program, the system partially observes TOU exceptions for this TOU exception program that exceed the billing period during billing. The period for a TOU exception is then prorated, for example as a result of a price change. If you do not select this indicator, the system does not observe TOU exceptions that exceed the billing period during billing and terminates billing. The period for the TOU exception cannot be split using proration dates in this case.

i Note You should ensure that splitting the TOU exceptions does not contradict the logical meaning of the TOU exceptions.

Title: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure
Section: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure > Monitor and Edit Time-of-Use Exceptions > Features
Document: doc_011

Content:
You can select the TOU exceptions you want to monitor or edit using a combination of different criteria, such as a user name, a specific period of time, an exception program ID, or an exception text. You can also restrict the number of TOU exceptions selected by making an entry in the Restrict Number To field. For more information about the possible selection criteria and the combinations available, see the documentation for the report REEXCEPTION DISP_MAINT.

Monitoring of TOU Exceptions

You can use the Change Layout function to add additional fields (such as administration data and texts). By selecting a line and choosing |}Goto » Exception Response 3, you can navigate to the available TOU exception responses for the selected TOU exception. Here, you can change or delete the responses, or you can change the activation status - see Monitor and Process Time-of-Use Exception Responses.

Creating TOU Exceptions

The From/To time information is in the same time zone as the selected TOU exception program. You can determine the predefined time period in the BAd| ISU_TOUEXCEPT_ TIME, method SET FROM TO DATE_TIME. If the activation category of the TOU exception program is not Active for Individual Customers, the TOU exceptions may not overlap. In addition, a TOU exception must be in the time period of the TOU exception program. The From/To time information must match the interval length of the appropriate TOU interface.

Note If the TOU exception program is not linked to a conditional billing program in Customizing, the check does not take place. Also note that the system does not check whether the TOU exception period is part of a period that has already been billed for a relevant installation.

When a TOU exception is created, the activation status is set to Active. You can determine the default status in the BAdI ISU TOUEXCEPT STATUS, method SET ACTIVATION STATUS When you create a TOU exception, the activation status (Active or Inactive) is set automatically.

Change TOU Exception

When you change a TOU exception, the system carries out the same checks that are carried out duing creation. You can only change a TOU exception if it has not yet been billed. You can view all changes to TOU exceptions by selecting a line and choosing Goto Change Document *¥. Note that the From/To time information is in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Also, the Text for TOU Exception Program field is not entered in the change document.

You can toggle between the status Active and Inactive by selecting one or more lines and choosing |}*Edit + Change Activation Status “Jin the menu. When you change the status, the system checks in the BAd| ISU TOUEXCEPT STATUS, method CHECK_CHANGE ACTIVATION STATUS whether the TOU exception has already been billed. If billing has been performed for the TOU exception, you can no longer change the activation status.

Delete TOU Exception

You can only delete a TOU exception if it has not yet been billed.

Enhancements

You can use the enhancement spot ISU TOUEXCEPTION to define enhancements.

Note Note that the report RETOUEXCEPTION DISP_MAINT is only intended for manual corrections on a small scale.

You can select the TOU exceptions you want to monitor or edit using a combination of different criteria, such as a user name, a specific period of time, an exception program ID, or an exception text. You can also restrict the number of TOU exceptions selected by making an entry in the Restrict Number To field. For more information about the possible selection criteria and the combinations available, see the documentation for the report REEXCEPTION DISP_MAINT.

Monitoring of TOU Exceptions

You can use the Change Layout function to add additional fields (such as administration data and texts). By selecting a line and choosing |}Goto » Exception Response 3, you can navigate to the available TOU exception responses for the selected TOU exception. Here, you can change or delete the responses, or you can change the activation status - see Monitor and Process Time-of-Use Exception Responses.

Creating TOU Exceptions

The From/To time information is in the same time zone as the selected TOU exception program. You can determine the predefined time period in the BAd| ISU_TOUEXCEPT_ TIME, method SET FROM TO DATE_TIME. If the activation category of the TOU exception program is not Active for Individual Customers, the TOU exceptions may not overlap. In addition, a TOU exception must be in the time period of the TOU exception program. The From/To time information must match the interval length of the appropriate TOU interface.

Note If the TOU exception program is not linked to a conditional billing program in Customizing, the check does not take place. Also note that the system does not check whether the TOU exception period is part of a period that has already been billed for a relevant installation.

When a TOU exception is created, the activation status is set to Active. You can determine the default status in the BAdI ISU TOUEXCEPT STATUS, method SET ACTIVATION STATUS When you create a TOU exception, the activation status (Active or Inactive) is set automatically.

Change TOU Exception

When you change a TOU exception, the system carries out the same checks that are carried out duing creation. You can only change a TOU exception if it has not yet been billed. You can view all changes to TOU exceptions by selecting a line and choosing Goto Change Document *¥. Note that the From/To time information is in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Also, the Text for TOU Exception Program field is not entered in the change document.

You can toggle between the status Active and Inactive by selecting one or more lines and choosing |}*Edit + Change Activation Status “Jin the menu. When you change the status, the system checks in the BAd| ISU TOUEXCEPT STATUS, method CHECK_CHANGE ACTIVATION STATUS whether the TOU exception has already been billed. If billing has been performed for the TOU exception, you can no longer change the activation status.

Delete TOU Exception

You can only delete a TOU exception if it has not yet been billed.

Enhancements

You can use the enhancement spot ISU TOUEXCEPTION to define enhancements.

Note Note that the report RETOUEXCEPTION DISP_MAINT is only intended for manual corrections on a small scale.

Title: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure
Section: SAP Utilities Billing Procedure > Archiving of Time-of-Use Exceptions > Features
Document: doc_011

Content:
The archiving process for TOU exceptions consists of the following steps:

1 Analysis of TOU exceptions with regard to potential archiving.
2 Archive the TOU exceptions selected in the first step.
3 Delete TOU exceptions from the database on the basis of the previously created archive.
4 Optional reloading of archived and deleted data.

Note Note that you cannot reload individual TOU exceptions, but must always reload the entire archiving run. This procedure should not normally be used and should be limited to extreme problem cases (for example, incorrect retention period in Customizing).

5 Optional reading of TOU exceptions from the archive and output in a list before the deletion process.
1 Analysis of Archivability of TOU Exceptions (report REAARCH_ANALYSE_EXCEPT)

First you restrict the archiving volume. To do this, enter the ID of the TOU exception program for which you want the TOU exceptions to be archived.

- Determination of Final Date for Archiving: The retention period in days in defined in Customizing for SAP Utilities under |*Tools » Archiving » Define Retention Period for Archiving Objects %. The system determines the final date for archiving from this retention period. You can only

archive documents whose existence exceeds the retention period defined in Customizing. The system uses the retention period for the archiving object ISU BILL (billing document header) to determine the final date for archiving TOU exceptions.

- Determine Billing Documents: TOU exceptions can only be archived if the billing documents for the corresponding TOU exception have been archived.
- Determine the TOU Exception Responses TOU exceptions can only be archived if the TOU exception responses for the corresponding TOU exception have been archived.
- Write Temporary Index: The system writes the TOU exception ID and the TOU exception program to the index table ETOUEXCEPTIONAR for the TOU exceptions that can be archived. This index table is used as the basis for archiving. Once data has been successfully archived and deleted, the system deletes the respective index entry from the database.
2 Archiving of Selected TOU Exceptions (Report REAARCH_ARCH_EXCEPT)

Content:
Before starting this archiving report, you must perform at least one analysis using the REAARCH_ ANALYSE EXCEPT report.

The archiving report selects TOU exceptions for which a corresponding entry exists in the index table ETOUEXCEPTIONAR, whose entries are generated by the analysis report. The system writes the entries found to the archive.

Note If you start the report in the test mode, the system does not write the data to the archive, and only displays an overview of the TOU exceptions that you can archive (if a detailed log display is required).

When you start the report you can make various settings on the initial screen:

- Archiving You can use this action to archive data for completed business objects. The system performs archivability checks to establish whether data can be archived. In this regard, this function is the same as standard data archiving. The ILM enhancements mean that during the write phase, the system can evaluate the rules maintained in the Information Retention Manager (IRM) for each object instance and therefore determine the retention period and the storage location

for the object. This information is persisted to the database as part of the administration data and is interpreted later during storage.

- Snapshots

lost, this type of session is not provided for data deletion. Therefore, snapshots always create redundant copies of data from the database. The snapshot function is mainly intended for use in conjunction with the ILM Retention Warehouse component when decommissioning older systems.

- Data Destruction This action destroys data from the database in an archiving write session and then in a subsequent delete run. This creates temporary archive files which the system deletes automatically with the file-related administration data at the end of the deletion phase. A run is classified as a destruction run in technical terms by the DESTROY parameter. If an archiving object has not been registered in the Information Retention Manager (IRM), the system ignores the DESTROY parameter and

executes a standard archiving session.

3 Deletion of TOU Exceptions from the Database (Report REAARCH_DEL_EXRESP)

Title: Automatic Billing
Section: Automatic Billing
Document: doc_012

Content:
Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer.

Use

Automatic billing enables you to bill a single contract or any selection of contracts. Contracts not allocated to an installation are not selected. Billing is executed based on intervals defined in scheduling. All master data that form the basis of the contract — such as the installation, device or register — are automatically taken into account.

Integration

Automatic billing provides a link between general master data and invoicing. In addition to general master data, the following billing master data are included in automatic billing:

- Rate Type
- Operand
- Price
- Price Adjustment Clause
- Rate
- Schema
- Rate Category
- Rate Determination
- Variants
- Discounts
- Franchise Fees

Scheduling determines how often billing runs occur. All billed contracts of a contract account can be invoiced, which is followed by printing of the bill.

Prerequisites

All master data and billing master data must be consistent before billing can be executed. This means the following:

- Abusiness partner and a contract must be allocated to the installation in move-in processing.
- Devices containing registers must be allocated to this installation in device installation.
- Meter reading orders must be generated and meter reading results must be entered in meter reading.
- The schedule records must be created in scheduling.

Features

Automatic billing determines the amount to be paid, based on the meter reading taken for the register. Calculation rules defined in variants in the rate are used to calculate this amount. Nonmeasured consumption and demand values specified in the facts for the rate, the rate category or the installation are also taken into account.

Activities

For more information, see:

- Billing Execution
- Simulation/Billing Simulation
- Simulation Execution
- Billing Simulation

Title: Budget Billing Plan
Section: Budget Billing Plan
Document: doc_013

Content:
Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer.

Use

Utility companies normally bill for their services at the end of a supply period - in an annual consumption billing, for example. Therefore, they charge budget billing amounts during the supply period instead of the actual amount owed, in order to remain solvent. You specify the budget billing amounts and the dates that are due in the budget billing plan. The budget billing plan is the basis for charging budget billing amounts. With budget billing plans, you manage the budget billing requests in a billing period in between two periodic bills. You can use several budget billing procedures. Each of these have different ways of determining budget billing dates and amounts, managing budget billing data, and posting procedures:

- Statistical budget billing procedure
- Partial bill procedure
- Payment plan procedure
- Payment scheme

Features

You can display and change active and inactive budget billing plans for a contract account. You can also display the following information:

- Start and end of budget billing plan
- Division
- Budget billing amount
- Billing period
- Premise
- Contract
