Content:
Use

If you want to charge interest on items to be dunned, you can link the interest calculation to a dunning level.

Features

If the calculation of interest on items to be dunned is defined for a dunning level, the dunning activity run calculates interest on items with this dunning level automatically. It does this using the item interest calculation application component. The interest calculation is based on the interest calculation rule of the interest key defined in the dunning level. The interest is posted in accordance with the specifications in the system settings for the dunning level.

Activities

To enable item interest calculation in the dunning activities run, you have to make the following settings in the Implementation

Guide for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable :

If necessary, define the interest key that you want to assign to the dunning level under Business TransactionsInterest Calculationltem Interest CalculationDefine Interest Keys . The interest key contains the interest calculation rules to be used for the interest calculation, and you can define these in the same section of the IMG in the activity Define Interest Calculation Rules . Activate the interest calculation in the dunning activity run and assign the interest key to the required dunning level of the dunning procedure. You do this by double-clicking on the required dunning level of the dunning procedure concerned under Business

In addition to interest, you can also levy various charges on your business partner. If you set the indicator Interest before Charges , you can define whether the interest is to be calculated before the charges in the dunning activity run. This is necessary, for example, if the amount of the charges is to be dependent on the interest calculated. To create this dependence, define a function module for event 0360 in the Implementation Guide for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable under Program Enhancements — Define Customer-Specific Function Modules . SAP delivers function module FKK_SPECIALCHARGE_0360 as an example implementation for such a calculation. This enables you to restrict the amount of the dunning charges if you levy dunning interest as well as dunning charges. Define the minimum interest amount that can be posted for a dunning notice. For detailed information, see the documentation for the corresponding fields.

The Display Dunning Run Exceptions ( F7575) app provides a detailed view of the exceptions that occurred for business partners in a dunning run.

Key Features

You select the required exceptions by using the available filters, such as Dunning Run Date, Dunning Run ID, and Business Partner. In the overview, you can jump to the detail view of the selected exceptions to track the errors that led to the exception.

Integration

In the Analyze Dunning Run Exceptions app, if you select a business partner for whom dunning exceptions exist in the overview and then choose Display Dunning Exceptions, you branch to the Display Dunning Run Exceptions app.

SAP Fiori Implementation Information

For information about implementation of the Display Dunning Run Exceptions app, see SAP Fiori Apps Reference Library.

Related Information

Analyze Dunning Run Exceptions

Section: FI-CA Dunning > Dunning > Industry Component Insurance (FS-CD)
Document: doc_026

Content:
The following dunning procedure types are supported:

- Individual Dunning Notices In an individual dunning notice, all items in a contract are considered independently of one another. This means that you

can have several dunning procedures for one contract.

- Collective Dunning In acollective dunning notice, all items in a contract are dunned with one dunning procedure.
- Multi-Collective dunning Multiple collective dunning can, in contrast to collective dunning, contain several collective dunning notices for one

business partner/insurance object relationship in parallel.

- Contract Dunning In a contract dunning notice, only one current dunning procedure exists at any one point in time. This refers to the

oldest item.

- Account Dunning All items due for dunning for a contract account are dunned on a cross-contract basis for account dunning.

The dunning procedures to be used are determined in the dunning proposal run and saved in the item.

Content:
To map and control the dunning processes that you require using the dunning program, you first have to define the specifications for the dunning parameters described in this section in Customizing. In Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, carry out the activities listed under Business Transactions in the section Dunning. See also the documentation for the activities, the individual fields, and the indicators. Define the required dunning parameters manually in the master records of the contract accounts and/or in the document. To do this, use the Create Contract Account and Change Contract Account transactions (CAA1/CAA2), the Manage Contract Accounts app (F5474), or the Post Document and Change Document transactions (FPE1/FPE2). In certain business transactions, the system can also enter dunning parameters in the contract account and/or document automatically. This enables you, for example, to default the dunning procedure when you are creating contract accounts. Using the BAPI BAPI_CTRACCONTRACTACCOUNT_ CREA, you can determine dunning locks.

Note For the industry components Public Sector Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable and Utilities, in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, you can define default values for dunning procedures and dunning locks that the system then enters in the document automatically during posting (see|)»Basic Functions » Postings and Documents Document Maintain Document Assignments Maintain Transactions for Public Sector Contract Accounting 4 or Maintain Transactions for IS-U). In the industry component Insurance, you can also define the dunning parameters for the insurance object and determine whether the dunning parameters of the contract account or insurance object are to apply. The dunning parameters defined for the document override the parameters in the master data.

The dunning proposal run evaluates the parameters and derives the actions to be carried out.

Title: FI-CA Dunning
Section: FI-CA Dunning > Dunning Activities
Document: doc_026

Content:
Definition

Measure taken when a specific dunning level of a dunning procedure is reached.

Structure

You define dunning activities in the Customizing activity Configure Dunning Activities by specifying a function module with a predefined interface. For the dunning activity key, specify the name of the dunning activity, the activity type, and the name of the function module that executes the dunning activity. For activities that support the printing of Print Workbench forms, you have to define an application form.

Note Note that the function modules for dunning activities for correspondence dunning use a different interface than the function modules for dunning activities for dunning open items.

Then assign the dunning activities to the dunning levels of a dunning procedure in the activity Configure Dunning Procedure. You can assign a dunning activity to different dunning levels of different dunning procedures as well assigning different dunning activities to one dunning level. When you execute the dunning activity run, the function modules defined for the activities for a dunning level are called up. Dunning activities are industry-specific. However, you can also define installation-specific activities. ee Example Possible dunning activities are:

- Creation of a dunning letter
- Creation of a note by a clerk
- Submission of items to a collection agency
- Termination of a contract
- Setting a lock
- Creation of collection work items
- Disconnection of a Service

Title: FI-CA Dunning
Section: FI-CA Dunning > Dunning Grouping
Document: doc_026

Content:
Use

You can use dunning groups to process items with the same attributes together (for example, to dun them together in one dunning notice).

Structure

The dunning grouping defines which attributes must agree for items to be dunned together. You can use all of the fields of the open item as grouping criteria (for example, business partner, contract account, currency, contract reference). You define these criteria in the Customizing activity Define Dunning Grouping . For example, you can create a dunning grouping using the criteria business partner, currency, company code, and dunning recipient . If you do not use the currency for the dunning grouping, you can also dun items with different transaction currencies together. In this case, the balances and the comparison with the limit amounts are run in the local currency of the company code. i Note For Insurance , you define the dunning grouping for the dunning variant in Customizing.

The dunning groups, which consist of the items belonging to the dunning groupings, are created in the dunning proposal run. The system checks the days in arrears and the amount limits for each dunning grouping separately. A dunning group is only dunned if it contains at least one item that would trigger a dunning notice. For additional receivables such as interest and charges, in the Rules for Additional Receivables under |)Business Transactions » Additional Receivables 3 in Customizing, you can define that these are not to trigger a dunning notice. In event 0306, you can also realize a grouping by dunning levels. See the documentation of the sample function module FKK_SAMPLE_0306 and SAP note 403244. For contract accounts with alternative dunning recipients, you have to enter the fields Alternative Dunning Recipient and Address Number for Alternative Dunning Recipient in all groupings. If you carry out cross-contract account dunning, the field Grouping for Dunning Notices should exist in the grouping. The company code group is a grouping field implicitly; you do not have to specify it in the grouping. If the grouping for dunnign notices is not maintained in the contract account, the entries for the grouping SPACE apply. Make sure that you also have a dunning grouping SPACE.

Example A business partner is in arrears with payments. The receivables due for dunning have different currencies. You want to send the business partner a dunning notice for each of these currencies. To do this, you have to define a dunning grouping in Customizing under |'Business Transactions » Dunning » Define Dunning Grouping | and then assign the field WAERS to this as a grouping criterion. You then have to define the grouping in the contract account of the business partner.

Title: FI-CA Dunning
Section: FI-CA Dunning > Dunning Charges
Document: doc_026

Content:
Definition

The charges are calculated automatically based on a charges schedule defined in Customizing. In this schedule, you define the currency-specific and creditworthiness-specific charges scales. To define a charges schedule, proceed as follows:

1 In the Customizing activity Define Charge Types for Dunning , define charges types.
2 In the Customizing activity Configure Charges Schedule for Dunning Procedure , define the required amount limits and rounding rules.
3 In the IMG activity Configure Dunning Procedures , assign the required charges schedules to the dunning levels.

With each charges schedule you can manage charges data for up to three charges types. For each combination of charges schedule and charges types, you can create charges lots that are amount-specific, currency-specific, and creditworthiness-specific. You can then use these to determine charges. You can also define a main and a subtransaction. You can levy dunning charges as absolute amounts, or as percentages. Percentages are applied to the dunning balance. In the subtransaction, you can define whether additional receivables should be considered in this balance. The dunning activity run posts the dunning charges defined in the charges schedule for each charges type of a dunning level automatically. From the main and subtransaction, each industry component can derive a statistics indicator that determines whether the charges are posted statistically or relevant to the general ledger. The charges documents are created in the events 0360, 0361, and 0362. See the documentation for the sample function modules FKK_SAMPLE_0360, FKK_SAMPLE_0361, and FKK_SAMPLE_0362.

Content:
To meet legal requirements of the public legal dunning procedure, you have to make special settings in Cutomizing and define specific events of the dunning program. The following contains instructions for dealing with the different problem issues.

For each item, the system is to post a separate interest document item. Interest is to be calculated on an monthly baseis for months started where the key date is in the calendar month.

Subitems are to be totaled before they are rounding according to the rounding rule in the interest conditions and then subjected to interest calculation.

Interest is to be calculated on cleared subitems if they were not cleared by the key date for the interest calculation

The base date for the interest calculation is to be moved to the day after the next working day using the factory calendar (grace period rule)

The due date of the interest document item should be on the day after the due date of the item, moved to the next working day

1 To do this, in the SAP menu, choose |}Periodic Processing » For Contract Accounts » Dunning » Dunning Proposal Run (transaction FPVA).
2 Enter a date and an ID that you can use to identify the run later.
3 On the General Selections tab, enter the parameters that the program should use to select the items to be dunned. Using the dynamic selections, you can select the fields of the item (table DFKKOP). For selecting business partners or contract accounts, you can also use preselections for master data. Using these preselections, the system checks the specified master records against the interval limits of the mass activity, as if you had

entered these as individual values for the business partner/contract account. In each interval, therefore, the system processes only those master records that are both within the interval limits and are part of the preselection. To switch back and forth between direct selection and preselection, choose the pushbuttons Ry Preselection (Switch to Preselection) and ay Direct Selection (Switch to Direct Selection) next to the input fields for the business partner and contract account. By choosing the (| Detail pushbutton, you can display the preselection that was entered.

4 On the Dunning Parameters tab, specify the following parameters required for the dunning notices:
  - Net due date of the items to be dunned (optional)
  - Date of issue of the dunning notices As the date of issue, enter the date on which you plan to print the dunning notices. The system proposes the current date. Using the issue date, the system determines the days in arrears for the item due and the interval to the last dunning notice for the business partner. Using execution variants, you can postprocess the dunning proposal on the basis of any company-specific criteria in

event 300. If you set the Start Activity Run indicator, when you start the dunning proposal run, the system automatically starts the dunning activity run as well.

Note that if you start the dunning activity run directly after the dunning proposal run, you can no longer postprocess dunning proposals.

5 Run the program. For more information, see Functions for Scheduling Program Runs. You can postprocess the dunning proposal. To do this, check the application log of the dunning proposal run. For example,

you can exclude individual dunning notices from the dunning activity run by reversing the relevant dunning notices. Or you can remove dunning blocks that have been set in error. After you have completed postprocessing, delete the relevant dunning proposal run in the menu under |}Environment Delete Dunning Proposal “. Then start a new dunning proposal run. You can start the dunning activity run directly afterwards by setting the Trigger Activity Run indicator, or you can start it manually in a separate step.

Note The dunning proposal run checks whether there is a dunning notice that has not been executed for a business partner in the system. If this is the case, the dunning proposal run does not create a new dunning notice and issues a warning in the application log. The dunning proposal run considers dunning reductions that result from dispute cases in SAP Dispute Management, for example. The system distributes the dunning reductions to the dunning groups in event 0335 and reduces the dunning balance by this amount. SAP provides the sample function module FKK_SAMPLE_0335_DISPUTE for the deduction of amounts from dispute cases. Define the module as an installation-specific function module for event 0335.

Section: FI-CA Dunning > Dunning Activity Runs
Document: doc_026

Content:
Use

Once you have executed the dunning proposal run successfully, start the second subprocess of the dunning run — the dunning activity run.

Prerequisites

1 You have successfully completed the dunning proposal run.
2 You have carried out the preparations required for creating dunning letters (see Creating Printed Records).

Key Features

The dunning activity run determines and runs the dunning activities defined in the dunning procedures and dunning levels. A dunning activity run relates only to those overdue items determined in a dunning proposal run. If the dunning activity run carried out a dunning activity successfully, it sets the print date in the dunning proposal. The print date is the same as the run date. If errors occurred during the execution of the dunning activities run, the system only sets the print date in some of the dunning headers. If the cause of the error is in the dunning proposal, you have to reverse the dunning notices concerned. If the cause of the error is in the dunning activity run, you have to correct the error and then start the dunning activity run again for this dunning proposal run. In this second run, the dunning activity run only processes the dunning notices that have not been executed yet, that

If you run the dunning activity run in simulation mode, you can also test the correspondence creation. If you simulate a run again, but print after the first simulation run, in the second simulation the correspondence container is filled again and you can repeat the print. However, if you do not print between two simulation runs, the data in the correspondence container is overwritten and you can only print once at the end.

Activities

You schedule and start a dunning activity run in the same way as for a dunning proposal run. On the tab page General Selections, enter the run parameters for the dunning proposal run that you want to execute and then schedule the program run. For detailed information, see Functions for Scheduling Program Runs. In the dunning activity run, you can revise the dunning activities defined in Customizing. In event 0351, you can add or delete dunning activities dependent on information from the dunning header (for example, business partner). The program does not process business partners and contract accounts, for which locks exist during the program run due to dialog processing. Depending on whether you choose the “Business Partner” or “Contract Account” as the parallelization object, the program records all business partners or contract accounts that could not be processed. The job that processes the last interval (this does not have to be the interval with the highest number) selects the business partners and contract accounts that were not processed during the first attempt. If the reason for the lock no longer exists at that time, these business partners or contract accounts are processed, and therefore there is no need to schedule the run again.

Key Features

To send dunning notices and payment forms with the dunning run, you provide application forms with the Print Workbench component. You then print the correspondence using the Correspondence component. The following form classes are delivered as standard:

- FI CA DUNNING NEW (Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable) with the sample application form FI_CA DUNNING SAMPLE_SF (Smart Form)
- IS _U_ CA DUNNING (industry components Utilities, Telecommunications)

Depending on the dunning activity, you can create documents for a dunning notice in two ways:

- The dunning activity run creates the documents using industry-specific or customer-specific dunning activities. SAP does not recommend this method.

component. In events 0770 and 0773, you can determine the recipient and address for a dunning letter dependent on the dunning level. i Note To avoid printing dunning notices that have already been reversed, always print the documents immediately after the dunning activity run.

Payment Forms

If you use the function modules *DUNNING PR CORR CONT 0350 as a dunning activity, you can also send a payment form for the dunned items and the related interest and charge documents with the dunning letter. If the activity for creating correspondence has not created a payment form number, you can assign the payment form number using the function module FKK_DUNNING PF_NO DET 0350. The internal and external payment form numbers are saved in the dunning header and can be used to assign the open items on payment receipt. You print using the Print Workbench. There, certain form classes, such as form class IS_U_ CA DUNNING, provide data in structure PAYMO (Attached Payment Media Output). You can print this data on the attached payment form. The application form itself can also trigger a special printout using a separate CALL FUNCTION OPEN FORM. Using a collection, you can print the application form and the payment form attached together (see also the documentation for the Print Workbench). For detailed information about creating payment forms, see Payment Forms.

Activities

1 Configure the application forms you need in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable under |}Basic Functions >» Print Workbench > Define Application Forms 3. For more information, see Processing Application Forms in

the documentation for the Print Workbench.

2 Assign the application form to the required dunning activity in the Customizing activity Configure Dunning Activities (see Business Transactions } Dunning Notices %).
3 Define the dunning activities in the individual dunning levels of the dunning procedure (see |*Business Transactions Dunning Notices » Configure Dunning Procedures 3%).

If you set the indicator Print All Items in Customizing for the dunning level (screen area History and Dunning Printing), you can include items that are due in the future (info items) in the printout. The info items are not displayed in the dunning history. To print the total of all items selected, you have to create the total in your dunning form in the Exit-During-Loop of level OPEN_ ITEM, print it, and then reset it in the Exit-After-Loop.

Section: FI-CA Dunning > Reversing a Dunning Run

Content:
Use

If a dunning activity run has not been performed correctly (for example, incorrect issue date), or if individual items of the dunning activity run have not been successfully posted, because, for example, individual business partners were locked by a parallel process, you can use the Mass Reversal of Dunning Notices function (transaction FPVC) to reverse a complete dunning proposal run or the dunning notices not run successfully, and to reset all entries with errors in the dunning activity run.

Key Features

The system resets either the whole run or the items that were not successfully posted and marks the relevant entries in the dunning history as being reversed. The system determines and reverses the charges and interest posted during the dunning activity run and resets the creditworthiness for the customer in question. To reset additional dunning activities, you have to define a function module for event 0395 for each activity. The reversed entries in the dunning history are not included in the dunning level determination for the next dunning proposal run.

Note

Note for the Industry Component Utilities Industry

The lock document created by the dunning notice is deactivated.

Activities

3 On the General Selections tab, specify the ID of the dunning proposal run that you want to reverse.
4 Execute the run.

For more information about scheduling the run, see Functions for Scheduling Program Runs.

Section: FI-CA Dunning > Dunning by Telephone > Key Features
Document: doc_026

Content:
If you define the function module FKK_SAMPLE_0350_TEL_ITEM as dunning activity in Customizing, the dunning activity run automatically includes business partners that receive a dunning notice in a telephone list. You can then use this list to contact the business partners concerned by telephone. To process the telephone list, you can use the Dunning Telephone List transaction (transaction FPDUTL) in the SAP Easy Access screen, under: |}Periodic Processing » For Contract Accounts » Dunning Notice 3. Several clerks can use this transaction simultaneously. If the call to the dunned business partner has been made, the clerk responsible can set the entry in the list to “Completed”. To give a business partner information during the telephone call, you can use the detailed information for an entry in the telephone list, for example, to access the account balance, to access the objects linked to the dunning notice, and to access another function that you call up installation-specific in event 9011. To document the communication with the business partner in the system, the clerk can also create customer contacts manually or automatically — depending on how the system is configured. If aclerk has removed an entry from the list for processing, this entry is locked for processing for other clerks. Once processing is complete, the clerk can set an entry to “Completed” again, or place it back in the list. When you reverse a dunning notice or a dunning run, the system can automatically delete entries in the telephone list. To do this, use function module FKK_SAMPLE_0395_TEL_ITEM in event 0395. The entry is deleted regardless of its status at this point. Using correspondence type 3003, you can use the correspondence recipient control to enter an alternative business partner in the telephone list.

Title: FI-CA Dunning
Section: FI-CA Dunning > Dunning History
Document: doc_026

Content:
In a dunning history, the system records all dunning data for each dunned item. There you can find out about the individual dunning steps. The dunning program uses the dunning history to determine the dunning levels. In the dunning history (transaction FPM3), you can see which items have been dunned for a particular area. The functions of the dunning history are protected by the following authorization objects:

- F_KKDU (Dunning in Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable)
- F_KKKO_BUK (Authorization in Company Code)
- F_KKKO_GSB (Authorization in Business Area)

(cross-contract account dunning), the system does not check the authorization group. The system issues a message informing you of how many dunning notices are not displayed due to missing authorizations. Using the authorization object F_KKDU, the system checks the dunning history for authorization for the activities Set Next Dunning Level and Reverse Dunning.

Note In the account balance and the document display, you can display the dunning history only for line items that have actually been dunned, that is, items for which you have already performed dunning activities. Items that were included in the dunning notice as info items (as described in Creating Printed Records) do not appear here.

For each business partner, the dunning history shows the name and address as standard. With a customer-specific module defined in event 4700, you can change this text to meet your requirements. You can display additional data fields by enhancing the customer includes of structure FEKMAKO_PLUS for the dunning header and those of structure FKKMAZE_STRUC for the dunning items. Afterwards, fill your additional fields using a customer module for event 0391 for the dunning header or event 0392 for the dunning items.

Related Information

Maintain Dunning Notices

Content:
Use

By displaying a dunning run, you can determine which dunning runs processed an item.

Prerequisites

The dunning activity runs to be displayed were successfully executed.

Procedure

1 Display the dunning history as described in Displaying Dunning Activities .
2 Place the cursor on the required dunning grouping (dunning header). In the menu choose |}'Goto » Dunning Items.
3 Place the cursor on the required dunning item and choose Display Dunning Runs or the menu |}Goto » Display Dunning Runs.

Result

In an information window, you see a list of the run date and identification of all dunning runs in which the selected item was dunned.

The system records all dunning data for each dunned item. Using the Maintain Dunning Notices (F3678) app you can manually intervene in the dunning processes.

Key Features

You use the Maintain Dunning Notices app to do the following:

- Display dunning notices
- Display dunning notice items
- Set the next dunning level for a dunning notice item
- Reverse dunning notices

SAP Fiori Implementation Information

In the SAP Fiori Apps Reference Library, see the details for the Maintain Dunning Notices app.

Title: FI-CA Dunning
Section: FI-CA Dunning > Valuating the Success of Dunning
Document: doc_026

Content:
Use

With the Success Valuation of Dunning mass activity, you can determine whether the dunnings that you executed in Collections Management and the dunning procedure or collection strategy you selected were successful.

Key Features

The determination of the success is not subject to a fixed logic and can be performed by an installation-specific function module for event 0393. SAP provides the sample module FKK_SAMPLE_0393 where, for example, each payment received within 7 days of dunning is seen as a100% success. Each further day of delay reduces the success percentage rate by 2.5%.

Example If EUR 100 is dunned, and a payment of EUR 70 is received after 7 days, and the remaining amount of EUR 30 is paid after 15 days, this results in a success percentage rate of 100% for EUR 70, and 80% for EUR 30. The weighted average is then 94%. The valuation run enters this value in the dunning history.

Activities

1.In the SAP menu, choose |}Periodic Processing » For Contract Accounts » Dunning > Success Valuation of Dunning (transaction FPVV).

2 Enter a date and an ID that you can use to identify the run later.
3 On the Selections tab page, you can restrict the dunnings to be selected by business partner and company code or the run parameters of one or more dunning runs.

A. Schedule the program run. For more information, see Functions for Scheduling Program Runs.

Title: FI-CA Dunning
Section: FI-CA Dunning > Creditworthiness
Document: doc_026

Content:
The system automatically determines the total creditworthiness of a business partner in returns processing and in a dunning run. The creditworthiness influences the activities and the charges levied, provided that you have defined the activities and charges dependent on creditworthiness in Customizing. There is a display and change function for creditworthiness. There are the following features:

- You can display the automatically determined creditworthiness of every business partner in a creditworthiness history. Using the creditworthiness history you can see an overview of when the creditworthiness of a business partner changed

(SAP menu: |}Account » More Information » Creditworthiness 4, transaction FPCR1).

- You can enter or change the creditworthiness manually. The manual creditworthiness is added to the value of the automatically determined creditworthiness, and thus forms the overall creditworthiness of a customer.
- You can enter a percentage creditworthiness factor for each business partner. You use this factor to weight the creditworthiness depending on the business partner.
- You can fix the current value of the automatically determined creditworthiness. The creditworthiness value can then only change for reasons relating to creditworthiness, such as dunning or dunning notice reversal, but not for time-dependent reasons.
- You can release this fixed value manually, so that the creditworthiness can change for time-dependent reasons.
- You can enter or reverse a creditworthiness record manually or with a BAPI in the creditworthiness history. The system then determines the new creditworthiness automatically.
- For the creditworthiness of a business partner, SAP delivers the object type CA_CRDRTNG and the BAPIs contained therein.

Change documents record any entries or changes that you have made to the manual creditworthiness, as well as changes to the percentage creditworthiness factor. If there is no data record for the current calendar year when you call the Change Creditworthiness function, the system automatically creates an initial record. The initial record contains the current calendar year. All other values in the creditworthiness records are blank.

You display and change the creditworthiness of a business partner in the SAP menu under |/*Master Data Business Partner Display Creditworthiness / Change Creditworthiness 4 (transactions FPCR1 or FPCR2) or in the Manage Creditworthiness app.

Content:
Compare Credit Score

With the Manage Creditworthiness (F4408) app you can display and change the creditworthiness of business partners.

You can use this app to:

- Display the creditworthiness of a business partner
- Change the creditworthiness of a business partner
- Track the creditworthiness of a business partner over time
- Fix the creditworthiness of a business partner

The system automatically determines the creditworthiness of a business partner in returns processing, in a dunning run, and during write-off. The creditworthiness influences the activities and the charges levied, provided that you have defined the activities and charges dependent on creditworthiness in the system configuration. The creditworthiness value consists of a manual and an automatic part. The automatic value is determined by multiplying the credit numbers of the processes relevant for creditworthiness (Such as dunning notices and returns) by the time-dependent credit weighting, and adding up the results. Creditworthiness is determined using the following formula: Creditworthiness = automatic creditworthiness value x percentage credit factor + manual creditworthiness The best creditworthiness value is O. This means that the business partner has a good payment history and has, for example, not been sent a dunning notice in the last few months. The worse the payment history of a business partner is, the higher is the creditworthiness value. The Manage Creditworthiness app displays the creditworthiness of business partners in a list. You can limit the results list by using filters. Once you have selected an entry from the list, the system displays all creditworthiness records, monthly totals, and the change history of the business partner. When you edit a business partner's creditworthiness:

- You can enter or change the creditworthiness manually. The manual creditworthiness is added to the value of the automatically determined creditworthiness. The result is the total creditworthiness of the business partner.
- You can change the percentage creditworthiness factor. You use this factor to weight the creditworthiness depending on the business partner. The percentage only refers to the creditworthiness portion that is determined automatically. The manual creditworthiness value is not affected. ee Example If you enter a percentage of O for a customer, the automatic portion of creditworthiness is not considered. In this case,

the creditworthiness value is that of the manual value.

- You can fix the current value of the automatically determined creditworthiness. The creditworthiness value can then only change for reasons relating to creditworthiness, such as dunning or dunning

- Under Creditworthiness Records, you can enter (create) a creditworthiness record manually. These manual entries you can reverse. The system determines the new creditworthiness automatically.

Change documents record any entries or changes that you have made to the manual creditworthiness, as well as changes to the percentage creditworthiness factor. If there is no data record for the current calendar year, the system automatically creates an initial record. The initial record contains the current calendar year. All other values in the creditworthiness record are blank.

Title: FI-CA Dunning
Section: FI-CA Dunning > Creditworthiness > Use
Document: doc_026

Content:
The creditworthiness of a business partner provides information on the business partner’s payment history and influences the selection of activities for dunning and/or returns and also the calculation of charges. Various different business transactions, such as returns, dunning notices, installment plans, and write-offs update the creditworthiness in the system automatically. You can also transfer a creditworthiness record from external systems or manually. By default, the FI-CA creditworthiness of a business partner is calculated as a weighted total of the creditworthiness figures from the past 48 months (maximum). You define the monthly weightings in Customizing. A creditworthiness of zero means that the business partner has an excellent payment history. The maximum value is 9999. At event 0400, you can override the default calculation of the FI-CA creditworthiness. The creditworthiness value of a business partner results from the following parameters:

- The calculation type of the total creditworthiness You define how the system determines the total creditworthiness in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable under |Integration » Financial Supply Chain Management Credit Management's Define Specifications for

Credit Management ; in the Calculation Type field. For more information about the calculation options, see the documentation for the field.

Caution If you change the calculation type from SPACE to another value or change the value to SPACE, you must execute the mass activity Replicate Creditworthiness (transaction FPCM2) to replicate the external creditworthiness again. The reason for this is that the external creditworthiness is reduced during replication by the FI-CA creditworthiness for

- The creditworthiness factor in percent
- Manual creditworthiness
- Number of dunning notices, returns, and write-offs

The creditworthiness figure is adjusted if a dunning notice or return is reversed.

Prerequisites Time-Dependent Weighting To determine the weighted total, enter a time-dependent creditworthiness weighting in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable under |}Business Transactions » Dunning 3 and/or |}Returns » Define Time-Dependent Creditworthiness Weightings

If you want to use scoring, enter the dunning activities and/or dunning charges in conjunction with a creditworthiness figure. The creditworthiness of a business partner provides information on the business partner’s payment history and influences the selection of activities for dunning and/or returns and also the calculation of charges. Various different business transactions, such as returns, dunning notices, installment plans, and write-offs update the creditworthiness in the system automatically. You can also transfer a creditworthiness record from external systems or manually. By default, the FI-CA creditworthiness of a business partner is calculated as a weighted total of the creditworthiness figures from the past 48 months (maximum). You define the monthly weightings in Customizing. A creditworthiness of zero means that the business partner has an excellent payment history. The maximum value is 9999. At event 0400, you can override the default calculation of the FI-CA creditworthiness. The creditworthiness value of a business partner results from the following parameters:

- The calculation type of the total creditworthiness You define how the system determines the total creditworthiness in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable under |Integration » Financial Supply Chain Management Credit Management's Define Specifications for

Credit Management ; in the Calculation Type field. For more information about the calculation options, see the documentation for the field.

- The creditworthiness factor in percent
- Manual creditworthiness
- Number of dunning notices, returns, and write-offs

Content:

You can use the following functions to submit receivables, make required postings, and process the exchange of information with collection agencies:

- Releasing Receivables for Collection
- Submission of Receivables to Collection Agency
- Processing and Managing Collection Items
- Recalling Submitted Receivables
- Forwarding Information to Collection Agencies
- Processing of Incoming Information from Collection Agencies

In the system receivables are submitted in two steps. First you have to release the items for collection. Then you can submit the released items. The collection items created are recorded in the system. You can carry out the release and submission of the items manually, automatically as a mass run, or automatically in other business transactions. The system can determine the collection agency to which the receivables are to be submitted automatically during release or you can specify a collection agency when you submit. For the submission, the system checks whether the items entered manually or selected by the release run have a status that permits submission. For each collection agency, it creates a list and/or a submission file with all information relevant for collecting the receivables and calls the corresponding API for the submission. You can generally submit all items with Receivable Released for Submission (01) or Receivable Called Back (09) status.

Document: doc_027

Content:
Use

Releasing individual uncollectible receivables for collection and resetting the release

You can select individual unpaid items by business partner, contract account, document, or net due date, and set them manually for a collection order. You can also manually reset releases that have already been made for collection for individual items of a business partner.

Activities

To release items for collection:

1 In the SAP Easy Access screen, choose |sAccount » Submit to Collections » Release Items for Collection (transaction FPO3E).
2 Enter the criteria that you want to use to select the items to be submitted. If you select the Only Items to Be Submitted indicator, the system displays only those items that you have not yet

submitted to a collection agency. If you set the Written Off Items indicator, the items of a business partner that have already been written off are also offered for release for collection.

3 Choose Continue.
4 Select the items that you want to release for collection and choose |Edit » Hold for Collection Order

As aresult, you have released the items for submission. Via|#Items » Refresh = you can update the display. This means that the released receivables are no longer displayed. Via |-ltems Other Receivables “jyou can select new items.

To reset the release:

1 In the transaction Release Items for Collection, select the required items.
2 In the menu, choose |Edit » Reset Release
3 Save your entry.

Use

Using the mass run Release for Collection is recommended if you are processing large volumes of data.

Activities

1 In the SAP Easy Access screen, choose |sPeriodic Processing For Contract Accounts » Submission for Collection Release Run 3 (transaction FPQ3M).
2 Assign a date ID and an identification that you can use to identify the run later and on the General Selections tab, restrict the selection of the receivables to be released. On the Additional Selection tab, you can refine this search using additional criteria and also include statistical and written off items in the selection. You can also restrict the selection using a run

variant according to your company-specific requirements (see also the documentation for the field Execution Variant and the section Releasing Receivables for Collection).

3 Choose whether you want to start a simulation run or actually release the receivables.

Document: doc_027

Content:
You want to release receivables for collection in other business transactions.

The release of receivables for collection is integrated in the following business processes:

- Dunning
- Write-off
- Write-off in mass run

If you make the relevant system settings, items that have reached a certain dunning level are automatically released for collection. If you select the Release Receivables for Submission to Collection Agency indicator during manual write-off or in the write-off run, the receivables written off are automatically released for collection. During the release, the programs determine the items to be released, release the positions, and set the submission status 01 (Receivable Released for Submission). The document is given the collection item number OO1. The collection agency is determined in event 5060.

Dunning

If you want to release items automatically in the dunning run, in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, under Business Transactions » Dunning Notices» Configure Dunning Activities “, define a relevant dunning activity and enter the function module FKK_COLL_AGENCY_RELEASE_0350 for this activity. The function module is processed in the dunning run. If the dunning level is reached, the module selects the items and releases them automatically. See also the documentation for the Customizing activity.

Write-Off

1 In the SAP Easy Access menu, choose |sAccount . Write Off Items “J (transaction FP04).
2 Then proceed as described in the section Writing Off Items.

Mass Write-Off

1 In the SAP Easy Access screen, choose |}*Periodic Processing » For Contract Accounts » Write-Off Run 3 (transaction FPO4M).
2 Then proceed as described in the section Writing Off Items in Mass Runs.

You can communicate with your collection agencies by using files (creation of submission and information files, import of collection agency files) or by using Enterprise Services or APIs. SAP provides the necessary APIs and Enterprise Services, and a service-oriented interface. If you activate the service-oriented interface, it replaces the file interface and offers the following additional functions:

- Groupings of collection items for submission, along with external grouping information (external collection cases or court cases), are supported by the application in the form of collection units.
- External status information on the progress of processing is integrated in the submitting company's own status information by using the collection history (SAP Easy Access screen: |»Account Further Information » Collection History

(transaction FPCOLLHIST).

- Pavments renorted by the collection agency result in the nostinge of receivables which are credited to the collection acencv.

1 To be able to use the service-oriented interface for submissions to collections, you have to activate it in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable. To do this, in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable,

choose either |*Integration } Enterprise Services Make Central Settings for Enterprise Services “J or |}Business Transactions » Submit to Collections » Activation of Communication Through API or Enterprise Service

Note For more information about the dependencies related to activating the service-oriented interface, see the documentation for the indicator you use to activate the service-oriented interface.

Caution If you previously communicated with collection agencies by file, do not activate communication via Enterprise Service/API until you have processed all the information that you received by file and stored in the system. After you have activated communication by using Enterprise Services or APIs, you can no longer process information that you have received by file and stored in the system. When communicating with collection agencies by using files, the system saves the exchanged information in a different table than when communicating with collection agencies by using the available Enterprise Services/APIs. If you switch to communication by using Enterprise Services/APls, you must migrate the data. To do this, in the SAP Easy Access screen, choose |Administration » Migrate Collection Items for Service Communication J (transaction FPO3MIG).

2 Then you make the necessary settings for collection agency postings in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable in the activities Define Specifications for Processing Collection Agency Information and Define Specifications

for Collection Agency Postings under |}/Business Transactions » Submit to Collection Agency

3 You enter the allowed status information about the progress of processing at external collection agencies in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, under |)«Business Transactions » Submit to Collection Agency » Define

Categories of Collection Units

4 You can classify collection units when you submit to collections; you enter the allowed categories in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, under |)Business Transactions » Submit to Collection Agency » Define

Categories of Collection Units

5 To display status information in the collection history, select the Coll. Hist. column in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, under |Business Transactions } Submit to Collection Agency + Define Submission Status J and

under Maintain Status of Collection Units.

6 In addition, define a variant for the collection history with the event 0007 Submit for Collection in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, under|}*Business Transactions » Dunning » Collection History » Define

Variants

Use

determine the collection agency to which the receivables are to be submitted for items released both manually and automatically. As a result of the release, the released items receive the submission status 01 (Receivable Released for Submission). The document receives the collection item number OO1.

Prerequisites

You have authorization to submit receivables to collection agencies (authorization object F_KKINK).

Activities

1 For the system to determine the collection agency automatically, specify the collection agencies you work with in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable under |sBusiness Transactions » Submit to Collection Agency Define Collection Agencies “J, or on the SAP Easy Access screen, choose |}Settings » Current Settings } Define

Collection Agencies

. Program an installation-specific function module and enter it for event 5060 in the Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable under |}#Program Enhancements » Define Customer-Specific Function Modules %. (See the documentation for function module FKK_SAMPLE_5060.) At event 5060, you can determine the collection agency, for example, using the following criteria:

  - Total amount of the receivables of a business partner to be released
  - Business partner type (private/business customer)
  - Business partner address (postal code)

In event 5060, you can also implement the determination of collection agencies from external systems and define the order in which receivables are to be submitted to the collection agencies that you work with. . The derivation tool is always called in function module FKK_COLL_AG SAMPLE 5060, if items are released for collection individually or in a mass release. The derivation tool determines the responsible collection agency in one or more derivation steps from a number of source fields of the extendable structure FKKCOLLAG. The number of derivation steps corresponds to the number of derivation rules that you define in Customizing. . In event 5059, which is processed when you release receivables, you can exclude items from being released. (See the documentation for sample function module FKK_SAMPLE_ 5059.)

Communicating with Collection Agencies by Using Enterprise

Services or APIs

Use

You can communicate with your collection agencies by using files (creation of submission and information files, import of collection agency files) or by using Enterprise Services or APIs. SAP provides the necessary APIs and Enterprise Services, and a service-oriented interface. If you activate the service-oriented interface, it replaces the file interface and offers the following additional functions:

- Groupings of collection items for submission, along with external grouping information (external collection cases or court cases), are supported by the application in the form of collection units.
- External status information on the progress of processing is integrated in the submitting company's own status information by using the collection history (SAP Easy Access screen: |sAccount Further Information » Collection History

(transaction FPCOLLHIST).

- Payments reported by the collection agency result in the posting of receivables which are credited to the collection agency. This means that the system posts these receivables to the contract account of the collection agency in FI-CA.

Activities

1 To be able to use the service-oriented interface for submissions to collections, you have to activate it in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable. To do this, in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable,

choose either |#Integration » Enterprise Services > Make Central Settings for Enterprise Services J or |}Business Transactions » Submit to Collections Activation of Communication Through API or Enterprise Service i Note For more information about the dependencies related to activating the service-oriented interface, see the documentation for the indicator you use to activate the service-oriented interface.

Caution If you previously communicated with collection agencies by file, do not activate communication via Enterprise Service/API until you have processed all the information that you received by file and stored in the system. After you have activated communication by using Enterprise Services or APIs, you can no longer process information that you have received by file and stored in the system. When communicating with collection agencies by using files, the system saves the exchanged information in a different table than when communicating with collection agencies by using the available Enterprise Services/APIs. If you switch to communication by using Enterprise Services/APls, you must migrate the data. To do this, in the SAP Easy Access screen, choose |sAdministration » Migrate Collection Items for Service Communication 9 (transaction FPO3MIG).

2 Then you make the necessary settings for collection agency postings in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable in the activities Define Specifications for Processing Collection Agency Information and Define Specifications

for Collection Agency Postings under |sBusiness Transactions } Submit to Collection Agency

4 You can classify collection units when you submit to collections; you enter the allowed categories in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, under |)»Business Transactions » Submit to Collection Agency » Define

Categories of Collection Units 9.

5 To display status information in the collection history, select the Coll. Hist. column in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, under |}Business Transactions » Submit to Collection Agency > Define Submission Status Jand

under Maintain Status of Collection Units.

6 In addition, define a variant for the collection history with the event 0007 Submit for Collection in Customizing for Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, under|}Business Transactions » Dunning > Collection History » Define

Variants J.

Related Information

Commissioned Outstanding Collections Processing

Title: Disconnection/Reconnection of a Utility Installation
Section: Disconnection/Reconnection of a Utility Installation
Document: doc_029

Content:
This component enables you to manage disconnections and reconnections. This component is optional. You need to use it if you want to temporarily interrupt supply to customers (especially within the bounds of a legal dunning procedure). A disconnection is a temporary interruption in the supply of a utility service that does not involve the meter removal. This is due to the following reasons, for example:

- Introduction of a collection procedure for outstanding payment
- Technical disconnection due to request of utilities company or customer

In the first instance, the service is resumed (reconnection) when the customer has paid the outstanding bill; in the second, it is done at the request of the customer.

Disconnections and Reconnections in an Advanced Metering Infrastructure Environment

If you are working in an advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) environment, you can find more information under Advanced Metering Infrastructure.

Notifying Customers of Upcoming Disconnections and Reconnections

Depending on legal requirements or on intra-enterprise guidelines, y ou might be required to contact your customers before you carry out a disconnection or reconnection. The customer contact process is called Notification. In such situations, you (or a CRM agent) need to execute additional steps between the disconnection or reconnection request and the actual disconnection or reconnection.

Invoicing

You can invoice flat-rate charges for a disconnection or reconnection using the SAP Utilities component (IS-U). For more information, see the Invoicing component. If you create a service order for the field service employee, and want to invoice the order then you require the Customer Service (CS) and Sales and Distribution (SD) components. For more information, see View: Customer Service (CS) and Plant Maintenance (PM) and Sales and Distribution.

Confirming Disconnection and Reconnection Order Data

You can confirm disconnection and reconnection order data in the system using the IDoc ISU DISC UPLOAD (IS-U/CCS: upload disconnection/reconnection order data). For more information about IDocs see the following documentation:

- For general information, see IDoc Interface/Electronic Data Interchange

If you disconnect a business partner because he/she has reached the disconnection dunning level, the system changes the creditworthiness of the business partner for each disconnection. To do this, go to Customizing under |}SAP Utilities 5 Customer Service » Process Execution » Disconnection/Reconnection Define Processing Variants for Disconnection Documents 4 and make an entry in the Creditworthiness Weighting field. The change is reversed if the disconnection that triggered it is canceled.

Content:
l You can modify event R720 (reference check for reconnection) in the Standard function module table (which can be found in Customizing for Financial Accounting (Fl)) via the program enhancement for contract accounts receivable and payable. This enables you to perform an amount check. You can find a reference for the program enhancement in the ISU_CECK_RECONNETION_R720 function module (trigger reconnection upon clearing).

Reconnection orders are created for disconnected devices and flat-rate installations in the same way that disconnection orders are created. You also specify whether you need to contact the corresponding customer ( Notification ) before you carry out the actual device reconnection. If notification is required, the system generates a notification work item . The CRM agent assigned to this work item must contact the customer, set an agreed date and close the work item before the reconnection order can be processed further If notification is not required, or if the notification work item is closed, you can continue processing the reconnection order You can also generate a corresponding service management (SM) service order (note however, that if notification is required, the system can only generate service orders after you have set the agreed date and the notification work item is closed).

Enter a meter reading for a disconnected meter — you can create a billing order with the billing transaction Interim billing for the affected devices.

Title: Disconnection/Reconnection of a Utility Installation
Section: Disconnection/Reconnection of a Utility Installation > Disconnection Order Generation
Document: doc_029

Content:
If you want to generate a disconnection order, the disconnection document must have a reference object containing devices or flat-rate installations in its data environment. In the event that open item accounting is blocked, the contract account must contain at least one current contract when the disconnection order is generated.

During generation of a disconnection order, you enter a planned disconnection date and the number of devices or flat-rate installations to be disconnected. The system proposes all potential disconnection objects from the data environment of the reference object. In the disconnection processing variant, you can determine whether this proposal is to be division-dependent (according to the items of the contract account that are relevant to disconnection). Disconnection orders cannot contain any installations or devices, for which a reason for guarantee of supply has been specified. The same is true for disconnection objects that are already disconnected. You can generate a disconnection order for devices that are allocated to installations other than the installation from the environment of the reference object. However, a warning will be displayed so that the disconnection will not inadvertently affect other customers.

When you create a disconnection order, you specify a planned disconnection date and time ( Plan. Disc. Date and Disc.Time fields), indicating when an agent (or the system — in the case of remote disconnections) is to process the device disconnection.

If notification is required, the system generates a notification work item . When the CRM agent assigned to this work item contacts the customer, the customer can agree to the planned disconnection date and time, or propose a different one. The final date and time agreed upon by both the CRM agent and the customer are called the agreed date and agreed time.

- The agreed date and time can equal the planned disconnection date and time
- The agreed date and time can be earlier than the planned disconnection date and time — in this case, the agreed date and time must fall on or after the current date and time.
- The agreed date and time can be later than the planned disconnection date and time — in this case, the agreed date must fall on or before:
  - The maximum agreed date — this date is calculated by adding the planned disconnection date to the maximum agreed offset

The maximum agreed offset and maximum notification offset are specified by way of the Customizing activity Define Processing Variants for Disconnection Documents. You access this activity by way of the following path: SAPUtilities + CustomerService » Process Execution } Disconnection/Reconnection

If notification is required, the CRM agent must contact the customer within a specified time period:

- The earliest date and time that the agent can contact the customer are defined as the notification start date and time.
- The notification due date and time that appears on an agent's work list is defined as the notification due date and time — note however that it is still possible to contact the customer after this date, if required.

These dates and times are calculated using the planned disconnection date and time — more specifically, the system subtracts the start date offset and due date offset from this date to determine the notification start and end dates. The start date offset and due date offset are specified by way of the Customizing activity Define Processing Variants for Disconnection Documents. You access this activity by way of the following path: |»SAPUtilities s CustomerService Process

When notification is not required, an agreed date is not set from the standpoint of the user — however in the backend, the system automatically sets the agreed date to equal the planned disconnection date. Therefore an agreed date is always set in the backend, whether or not customer notification is required.

Devices selected in the disconnection order are always disconnected on the agreed date , since it is set, either by customer notification or by automatic mapping to the planned disconnection date.

Once an agreed date has been set, you can complete the disconnection order. Choose the Save button to save the order. If an order code and PM plant order number are provided, the system generates a service order, which can be processed by a service technician.

Generating Customer Notifications

In the disconnection order, you need to indicate whether a CRM agent is required to contact the corresponding customer before a service agent (or the system — in the case of remote disconnections) carries out the actual device disconnection. The process of contacting a customer for this purpose is called notification and the requirement for notification is based on legal requirements or on intra-enterprise guidelines.

- If notification is required, the system generates a notification work item . The CRM agent assigned to this work item must contact the customer, set an agreed date and close the work item before the disconnection order can be processed further.
- If notification is not required, or if the notification work item is closed, you can continue processing the disconnection order.

Creating and Managing Work Items and Worklists for Customer Notifications

- 21400001 - Disconnection notification agent
- 21400002 - Disconnection notification group
- 21400003 - Disconnection notification department

You can create a simple model using the report Create Organizational Model in ERP.

Automatic Assignment When Work Items are Created

To have automatic assignment when work items are created, you have to enter the responsibilities. On the SAP Easy Access screen, choose |*Periodic Processing For Contract Accounts + Dunning Notice 5 Areas of Responsibility

- Maintain Department Responsibilities
- Maintain Unit Responsibilities
- Maintain Collection Specialist Responsibilities

Item Management)

In this transaction, the manager of a department or group can perform the following tasks:

- Create worklists manually
- Change attributes of a worklist
- Display work items
- Assign work items to new processors or groups
- Change the starting time of work items

Temporary Release of Additional Users for Managing and Processing Worklists

- You can temporarily release additional users for managing worklists, without having to change the organizational model. To do so, on the SAP Easy Access screen, choose |}PeriodicProcessing » For ContractAccounts } Dunning » Areas

ofResponsibilities » Define Additional Department or Group Head The work items are processed in the CRM system in Financial Customer Care (FCC).

- You can temporarily release additional users for processing worklists, without having to change the organizational model. To do so, on the SAP Easy Access screen, choose |}Periodic Processing For ContractAccounts » Dunning » Areas ofResponsibilities + Define Additional Collection Specialist

Generating Service orders and Service Notifications

You can generate a Service order or a service notification in the Service Processing (CS-SE) component that corresponds to a disconnection order in an IS-U disconnection document (note however, that if notification is required, the system can only generate service orders after you have set the agreed date and the notification work item is closed).

Content:
- Customer requests — changing the agreed date

- Internal requests or requirements — rescheduling the planned date It is possible to change the planned disconnection date by way of the rescheduling process. For example, you might not have any technicians who are available to visit the disconnection site on the original agreed date. In this case, you will need

to reschedule the visit and thus, need to change the planned disconnection date. Rescheduling therefore, is defined as the modification of the planned disconnection date and is typically initiated by the utilities provider and not by the customer. For more information on rescheduling a planned disconnection, see Rescheduling of Disconnection and Reconnection Orders.

Note that is is not possible to change either of the the disconnection dates (agreed date or planned date) if a service order has already been generated.

Content:
Use

During the disconnection entry, you inform the system when and how which devices and flat-rate installations were disconnected. Disconnection entry can also include confirmation of the corresponding disconnection order.

Integration

When entering disconnections, you can:

- Post charges
- Enter meter reading results for disconnected devices
- Change budget billing plans

Prerequisites

You can maintain parameters for the disconnection entry in Customizing for the disconnection processing variant. You can for example define whether budget billing plan change are admissible or whether disconnection charges are to be levied.

The disconnections that have been documented are then observed, for example in the following transactions:

- Display Installation
- Change Installation
- Display Device
- Change Device

They are also observed during the following:

- Meter reading
- Billing
- Extrapolation
- Device replacement

You can disconnect disconnection objects in several disconnection documents simultaneously. The reconnection is not actually executed until the last reconnection request is received.

Activities

Confirmation of the optional service order generated

The disconnection is usually entered using the Change Disconnection Document transaction. However, you can also define it as a workflow step.

e takes place directly in Service Management

- Can be done directly in disconnection entry
- Can be controlled by making the corresponding settings in Customizing.

In Customizing under Utilities Industry . Customer Service — Process Execution = Disconnection/ Reconnection — Define Processing Variants for Disconnection Documents, you can specify that the service orders or service notifications are to be closed. In the individual confirmation status, you can define whether service orders are to be set to technically closed or not performed. Service notifications are always closed if this has been defined in Customizing.

Disconnection Document

Use

The disconnection document is automatically generated when the disconnection dunning level is reached. It contains all the items that reach the disconnection dunning level during a dunning print run. Generally the devices for disconnection are proposed from all the contracts belonging to a contract account. This makes the contract account the reference object of the disconnection document. A processing variant is uniquely allocated to each processing variant. It contains default values for the disconnection document functions and is configured in Customizing. The variant is assigned a unique disconnection reason and a long text. The disconnection document guarantees consistency in the overall disconnection and reconnection business process. A reconnection cannot be performed without a disconnection having occurred beforehand. If a disconnection has already been carried out on a device or flat-rate installation, a new disconnection order cannot be generated for this disconnection object. The disconnection/reconnection orders are confirmed in the disconnection document. They are assigned a status. Disconnection actions that have already been carried out can be reversed via the disconnection document (note that can only been done successively from the last action to the first).
